THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | QA Verification Standard — Mesh & Resolution | rev 3 | Effective 07/01/2025

Document ID: CFDME-QA-VS-MR Revision: rev 3 Effective Date: 07/01/2025 Supersedes: rev 2 (Effective
03/15/2023) Author of Record: Marguerite Falk, PE — Technical Director & Reviewing Engineer, AZ PE #42798
Applies To: All CFD deliverables issued from The CFD Mechanical Engineer, LLC (The CFD ME), 4820 E River Rd,
Suite 220, Tucson, AZ 85718


1. Purpose & Scope
This standard establishes the firm's minimum requirements for demonstrating that a CFD result is grid-independent
(for steady Reynolds-averaged work) or adequately resolved (for large-eddy simulation), and specifies how the
underlying evidence must be presented in the Verification section of every deliverable that leaves the firm.
The standard applies to every project executed by The CFD ME staff and to every subcontracted deliverable
prepared on the firm's behalf, including work performed by Mulshi Simulation Labs and any other external contractor
operating under a CFD ME work order. Reviewing Engineer sign-off on the peer-review checklist requires explicit
confirmation that the requirements of this document have been met.
Revision 3 rewrites the LES portion of the standard. The rev 2 language treated the Roache/Richardson grid
convergence index (GCI) as the default verification instrument for every solve regardless of turbulence treatment.
Two internal audits and a client peer review in Q1 2025 established that the treatment is technically incorrect for
large-eddy simulation and produces verification evidence that will not survive third-party scrutiny. The corrected
treatment is set out in Sections 4 and 5.
Nothing in this standard modifies the firm's Validation QA Procedure & Acceptance Criterion
(Firm/QA/CFDME_Validation_Procedure_rev2), the firm's Modeling Standards for Fire & Buoyant Flows
, current revision, or the Units and Conversions SOP
(Firm/Standards/CFDME_Units_SOP_rev2). Where the requirements of this standard intersect those documents, all of them
apply concurrently.

2. Definitions
Grid convergence index (GCI). A quantitative estimator of numerical uncertainty attributable to spatial discretisation
error, computed from a monotonic sequence of solutions on systematically refined grids under an assumed observed
order of accuracy. Reported as a percentage band on a selected integrated quantity of interest. The GCI is defined
for solutions that converge to a unique grid-independent limit as the mesh is refined.
Plume resolution index (D*/dx). The ratio of the characteristic plume diameter D* to the representative fire-region
cell edge length dx. D* is the buoyancy-driven length scale associated with a fire heat release rate Q_dot and is
defined as
D* = ( Q_dot / ( rho_inf · cp · T_inf · sqrt(g) ) )^{2/5}
where rho_inf, cp and T_inf are the ambient density, specific heat and absolute temperature respectively, and g is
gravitational acceleration. The index D*/dx is the standard measure of how many cells span the buoyancy-dominated
length scale of a fire plume.
Resolved turbulent kinetic energy (k_res). The turbulent kinetic energy carried by the explicitly resolved velocity
fluctuations in a large-eddy simulation, distinct from the sub-grid-scale contribution k_sgs modelled by the closure.
The resolved fraction is defined as k_res / (k_res + k_sgs).
RANS and steady work. In this document, "RANS and steady work" means Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes
simulations run to steady state, whether solved with a pseudo-time or true-steady solver, including internal buoyant
airflow of the type in the Copperline municipal HVAC envelope. Unsteady RANS (URANS) is treated as RANS for the
purposes of Section 4.
LES. Large-eddy simulation, including the firm's reacting-fire LES stack (fireFoam with EDC combustion and fvDOM
radiation) and any non-reacting LES of atmospheric or building flow.

3. General Requirements for Verification
Every deliverable that reports a CFD result shall contain a Verification section, plainly labelled as such, appearing in
the body of the report ahead of Validation and ahead of Results. The Verification section shall state, at minimum:
 (a) The turbulence treatment used (RANS, URANS, or LES) and, for LES, the sub-grid-scale closure.
(b) The representative cell edge length dx in the region of interest, and the total cell count.
(c) The verification basis chosen from Section 4 or Section 5, together with the numerical evidence supporting that
basis.
(d) A single-sentence statement identifying which acceptance criterion has been met and by what margin.
The Verification section shall not be an appendix pointer. Numerical values that support the verification claim shall
appear in the body. Supporting figures, residual histories, and mesh-slice imagery may be relegated to an appendix
and referenced.
Verification is prerequisite to Validation. A deliverable whose Verification section is absent, incomplete, or
inconsistent with this standard shall not be released for client transmission and shall not carry a Reviewing Engineer
signature.

4. Grid Convergence Index (GCI)
The Roache/Richardson grid convergence index is the firm's verification instrument for RANS and steady work only.
GCI is not valid for LES and shall not be used to verify any large-eddy result issued from this firm.
The reason is physical. Under systematic mesh refinement, an LES does not converge to a unique grid-independent
solution. As the filter width narrows, energy migrates from the modelled sub-grid-scale contribution into the explicitly
resolved field; the resolved-to-modelled turbulence split changes with the mesh. A three-grid sequence of LES
solutions therefore records a change in the physical content of the simulation between grids rather than a
discretisation-error tail collapsing toward a limit. The Richardson extrapolation on which the GCI is built assumes that
limit exists. It does not exist for LES, and therefore GCI values computed from an LES three-grid study are
numerically well-formed but physically meaningless. Non-monotonic behaviour in an LES three-grid quantity of
interest is the expected signature of the changing split, not evidence of a defective mesh study.
For RANS and steady solves, the firm applies the standard Richardson formulation. Given three systematically
refined grids with representative cell sizes h_1 < h_2 < h_3, refinement ratios r_21 = h_2 / h_1 and r_32 = h_3 / h_2
each at least 1.3, and a scalar quantity of interest phi with values phi_1, phi_2, phi_3 on the three grids, the observed
order of accuracy p is obtained from
phi_3 − phi_2 = ( r_32^p − 1 ) / ( r_21^p − 1 ) · ( phi_2 − phi_1 )
solved for p by fixed-point iteration. The fine-grid GCI on the finest pair is then
GCI_fine = F_s · | ( phi_2 − phi_1 ) / phi_1 | / ( r_21^p − 1 )
with a safety factor F_s of 1.25 when three or more grids are used. Reported GCI values shall carry the safety factor
and the observed p, and shall state the quantity of interest to which they apply. Monotonic convergence is a
precondition for reporting a GCI; oscillatory or divergent triples shall be flagged and the mesh study extended rather
than reported as a GCI band.
The requirement in this Section 4 applies without exception in the RANS envelope. Verification of a steady RANS
solve without a reported GCI (or an equivalent Roache/Richardson estimator) is not accepted.

5. LES Resolution Acceptance
For large-eddy simulations, the firm accepts either of the following as sufficient evidence that the resolution is
adequate in the fire or plume region of interest. Both are preferred; either alone is acceptable.
5.1 Plume resolution index. The plume resolution index D*/dx, computed with D* from the definition in Section 2 and
dx taken as the representative cell edge length across the buoyancy-dominated region, shall fall in the band 5 to 10.
Values below 5 are insufficient to carry the buoyancy-driven length scale; values above 10 are wasteful of compute
without corresponding gain in fidelity for the classes of fires the firm simulates. Q_dot in the D* expression is the fire
heat release rate applied in the LES, in watts.
5.2 Pope resolved-TKE criterion. The resolved turbulent kinetic energy shall be at least 80% of the total turbulent
kinetic energy in the region of interest, i.e.
k_res / ( k_res + k_sgs ) >= 0.8
 This is Pope's criterion for a well-resolved LES. The ratio shall be computed on a time-average of a statistically
converged solution window (typically ten or more integral time scales, or ten or more puffing cycles for a pool-fire-like
plume). Point probes shall be located within the buoyancy-dominated flow, not on the periphery of the domain.
Either criterion, met, is acceptable. Meeting both is preferred and is the default expectation for deliverables prepared
for authorities-having-jurisdiction or life-safety end use. Neither criterion may be evaded by asserting engineering
judgement in place of the numerical evidence; where a physical constraint prevents meeting either criterion, the
constraint and its consequence shall be stated explicitly in the Verification section and the deliverable escalated to
the Reviewing Engineer before release.

6. Reporting
The Verification section of every LES deliverable shall state, directly in the body of the report:
• The fire heat release rate Q_dot used to compute D*, with units.
• The characteristic plume diameter D*, with units.
• The representative cell edge length dx in the region of interest, with units.
• The plume resolution index D*/dx as a dimensionless number.
• The Pope resolved-TKE fraction k_res / (k_res + k_sgs) as a percentage, together with the location of the probe(s)
   and the length of the averaging window.
These values shall appear in the running text or in a table in the Verification section itself. Placement of any of these
values in an appendix, with only a cross-reference in the Verification section, does not satisfy this standard.
GCI values shall not appear in LES deliverables. A three-grid table copied forward from a RANS template into an
LES report, whether or not it is accompanied by a GCI band, is a non-compliant Verification section under this
standard. If a three-grid mesh study has been carried out on an LES case for information (for example, to
demonstrate insensitivity of an integrated quantity), the tabulated values may be included in an appendix labelled as
a sensitivity study, but they shall not be presented as verification evidence and no GCI shall be computed from them.
The Verification section of a RANS or steady deliverable shall state the observed order of accuracy p, the fine-grid
GCI on the reported quantity of interest with its safety factor, and the refinement ratios. D*/dx and Pope's criterion do
not apply to RANS deliverables and shall not be reported there.

7. Roles
Project Engineer. Responsible for constructing the mesh study or resolution assessment appropriate to the
turbulence treatment, computing the required indices, and drafting the Verification section in accordance with
Sections 3, 4, 5 and 6.
Reviewing Engineer. Responsible for confirming, on the peer-review checklist, that the Verification section of the
deliverable meets the requirements of this standard. The confirmation is a specific line item on the checklist and shall
not be a general "verification section reviewed" tick. For an LES deliverable, the Reviewing Engineer shall confirm
that D*, dx, D*/dx, and the Pope resolved-TKE fraction appear in the body of the report and that no GCI value has
been carried forward from a RANS template. For a RANS or steady deliverable, the Reviewing Engineer shall confirm
the presence of the observed order p, the GCI band and its safety factor, and monotonic convergence of the
underlying triple.
Owner / Principal Engineer. Retains final responsibility for the stamped CFD thermal analysis and for any release of
a deliverable in which the Reviewing Engineer has flagged a Verification-section deficiency that has not been
resolved.

8. References
1. Roache, P. J. (1994). Perspective: A Method for Uniform Reporting of Grid Refinement Studies. Journal of Fluids
Engineering, 116(3), 405–413. 2. Roache, P. J. (1997). Quantification of Uncertainty in Computational Fluid
Dynamics. Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics, 29, 123–160. 3. Richardson, L. F. (1911). The Approximate
Arithmetical Solution by Finite Differences of Physical Problems. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A,
210, 307–357. 4. Celik, I. B., Ghia, U., Roache, P. J., Freitas, C. J., Coleman, H., & Raad, P. E. (2008). Procedure for
Estimation and Reporting of Uncertainty Due to Discretization in CFD Applications. Journal of Fluids Engineering,
130(7), 078001. 5. Pope, S. B. (2000). Turbulent Flows. Cambridge University Press. (Chapter 13, resolved-TKE
 criterion for LES adequacy.) 6. Pope, S. B. (2004). Ten questions concerning the large-eddy simulation of turbulent
flows. New Journal of Physics, 6, 35. 7. McDermott, R., McGrattan, K., and Hostikka, S. (2008). Fire Dynamics
Simulator (FDS) Technical Reference Guide — Verification. NIST Special Publication 1018 (definition and use of the
plume resolution index D*/dx). 8. ASME V&V 20-2009 (R2016). Standard for Verification and Validation in
Computational Fluid Dynamics and Heat Transfer. 9. AIAA G-077-1998 (R2002). Guide for the Verification and
Validation of Computational Fluid Dynamics Simulations. 10. The CFD ME. CFD Modeling Standards — Fire &
Buoyant Flows, current revision. 11. The CFD ME. Validation QA
Procedure & Acceptance Criterion rev 2 (Firm/QA/CFDME_Validation_Procedure_rev2). 12. The CFD ME. External
Standards Digest, current revision.

P5: MEMORANDUM — PHASE 1 SCOPING
P7: 1.  Purpose & Scope
P8: This memo fixes, at project kickoff and before any meshing is undertaken, the first-principles basis on which the Phase 1 wildfire-exposure large-eddy simulation set will be built. It records the design conditions taken from the site meteorological pull, the buffelgrass fuel model, the Rothermel-to-Byram source-term chain that produces the design fire, the Froude regime assessment inputs, and the LES sub-domain geometry against which downstream mesh sizing will be measured. It is issued on the effective date of the Ocotillo Additive Structures Phase 1 Statement of Work (CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01, signed 10/08/2025), before revC of the assembly geometry (OAS-WUI-01_revC, transmitted with the SOW) is imported into the mesher.
P9: The intent is that every downstream case-setup artifact, mesh-study artifact, and Phase 1 reporting deliverable — including the interim hand-calc due 10/13/2025 and the LES setup deliverable due 10/20/2025 — trace their source-term, regime, and geometry inputs back to the numbers recorded here, rather than re-argue them case-by-case. Where a downstream artifact needs the design fire heat release, the characteristic source diameter, or the plume length scale, it shall cite this memo.
P10: The scope of Phase 1 as procured under Section 3.1 of the SOW is six transient wildfire cases (240 deg and 270 deg wind directions at 20-ft wind speeds of 5, 8, and 12 m/s). The fire source term and the sub-domain sizing recorded here apply to that entire matrix; they are not per-case parameters.
P11: 2.  Site Design Conditions
P12: Design conditions are taken from the ten-year hourly record of the Pima County ALERT network for the Avra Valley WUI corridor west of Tucson (data pull: site_met_avra_valley_2015-2024.csv, Section 3.1 of the SOW envelope). The following envelope governs Phase 1:
P14: These conditions define the site for regime classification (Section 4 below) and for the source-term chain (Section 3 below). They are the same conditions carried into the Phase 1 report; no re-derivation is required.
P15: 3.  Fuel Model — Sonoran Buffelgrass at Site Design Conditions
P16: The design fire source term is developed under the Rothermel spread-to-Byram intensity chain, evaluated at the site design conditions of Section 2. The buffelgrass fuel model is adopted per the SOW Section 2 definition (“Buffelgrass Fuel Model”). Fuel-model quantities are:
P17: •  Fuel load (dry):  w = 0.6 kg/m²
P18: •  Low heat of combustion:  h = 18,600 kJ/kg
P19: •  Rate of spread at design wind:  R = 0.9 m/s
P20: R is the head-fire rate of spread produced by the Rothermel surface-fire spread model for cured buffelgrass at the low-humidity, high-temperature, moderate-wind conditions of Section 2. It is used here as the input to the Byram fireline-intensity relation; the Rothermel-model input parameter tabulation for buffelgrass is on file with the project data pull.
P21: Byram’s fireline intensity is the product of the low heat of combustion, the available fuel load per unit area, and the rate of spread:
P22: I = h · w · R
P23:   = (18,600 kJ/kg) × (0.6 kg/m²) × (0.9 m/s)
P24:   = 10,040 kW/m
P25: The Byram wind-tilted solid-flame length correlation gives:
P26: L = 0.0775 · I^0.46
P27:   = 0.0775 × (10,040)^0.46
P28:   = 5.4 m
P29: L above is the wind-tilted Byram flame length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height and is not comparable to Heskestad’s still-air correlation (see Section 5 for the idealization record).
P30: 4.  Froude / Regime Assessment
P31: Regime selection follows CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §2. The controlling non-dimensional group is the Froude number formed on the characteristic source diameter of the LES sub-domain:
P32: Fr = u_wind / sqrt(g · D_char)
P33: Taking D_char = 3.0 m (the LES sub-domain segment fixed in Section 5 below) and g = 9.81 m/s²:
P34: sqrt(g · D_char) = sqrt(9.81 × 3.0) = sqrt(29.43) = 5.42 m/s
P35: Evaluated across the site design wind envelope 5–12 m/s:
P37: The Froude / plume-velocity ratio falls in the range ~0.9–2.2 across the entire design envelope.
P38: Regime classification.  Classification against the Modeling Standard §2 thresholds, and solver selection per §3 of that standard, shall be carried out and documented in the case setup record before any case in this matrix is meshed.
P39: This classification is made once, at the firm level, for the entire Phase 1 wildfire matrix; it is not re-argued case-by-case within the envelope.
P40: 5.  LES Sub-Domain
P41: The LES sub-domain represents a 3.0 m segment of the flaming front. This segment length is the characteristic source width used for the plume model, and the value of D_char used in the Section 4 Froude computation and in the plume-length-scale computation below.
P42: 5.1  Line vs Axisymmetric Reconciliation
P43: The Byram fireline-intensity relation of Section 3 gives an intensity per unit length of the fire front (kW/m). The plume length scale D* referred to by the firm modeling and verification standards is an axisymmetric-source property (kW total). The two quantities are not interchangeable and cannot be composed directly. The 3.0 m segment length is the specific conversion factor between them for this project: it defines how much fire-front length is captured within one LES sub-domain, and therefore what total heat release rate the plume model sees.
P44: Design fire heat release rate for the sub-domain:
P45: Q = I × L_segment
P46:   = (10,040 kW/m) × (3.0 m)
P47:   = 30,120 kW
P48:   = 30.1 MW
P49: Idealizations recorded so they are not misread as physical dimensions.
P50: •  Flame depth and flame residence time are not resolved in this sub-domain. The flaming front is represented as an equivalent 3.0 m characteristic-diameter source patch.
P51: •  The wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m from Section 3 is a wind-tilted correlation length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height. Heskestad’s still-air flame-height correlation, evaluated for the same 30.1 MW heat release rate at a 3.0 m diameter source, gives roughly 11.5 m. The 5.4 m vs 11.5 m gap between the two correlations is not treated as a discrepancy between two attempts to model the same quantity.
P52: Plume characteristic diameter D*.  For Q = 30.1 MW and standard reference-atmosphere conditions (ρ_∞ = 1.204 kg/m³, c_p = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, T_∞ = 293.15 K, g = 9.81 m/s²):
P53: D* = ( Q / ( rho_inf · c_p · T_inf · sqrt(g) ) )^(2/5)
P54:    = ( 30,100 / ( 1.204 × 1.005 × 293.15 × 3.132 ) )^(2/5)
P55:    = ( 27.08 )^(2/5)
P56: D* = 3.76 m.
P57: The fine-grid cell size specified for the LES mesh study is dx = 0.5 m (the finest of the three grids in the mesh study). This gives:
P58: D* / dx = 3.76 / 0.5 = 7.5
P59: which confirms the plume is adequately resolved on the fine grid. LES resolution acceptance shall be assessed per the firm QA standard applicable to reacting-plume LES.
P60: 6.  Wall Assembly Note
P61: The through-wall response of the assembly cannot be modelled as heat conduction through a single solid slab. Per the OAS-WUI-01_revC wall assembly section (Geometry/OAS_wall_assembly_section.png), the assembly is a double-wythe cavity system: two 50 mm printed-concrete leaves separated by a 205 mm open-air cavity (overall thickness 305 mm), tied together by continuous 9-gauge (3.8 mm) galvanized truss-type steel ties spaced 600 mm on centre vertically, embedded 25 mm into each leaf. The cavity carries no insulation. The architectural drawing (OAS_wall_assembly_section.png) uses the drawing-side identifier OAS-WA-305mm-DW in its title block; this refers to the same physical wall assembly as the engineering geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC used throughout the SOW, this memo, and all downstream analysis artifacts.
P62: The metallic ties are a continuous parallel thermal path between the exposed and unexposed leaves; their conductivity (~45 W/m·K) is more than an order of magnitude above the siliceous-aggregate concrete of the leaves, and they are the reason the single-point criterion governs over the average-rise criterion in the ASTM E119 test result of record.
P63: Per CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §6, the through-wall modeling treatment for this assembly shall be selected and documented in the case setup record before meshing, accounting for the metallic ties’ thermal-bridge role identified above. Temperature-dependent solid properties (k, ρ, c_p) apply per Modeling Standard §3.5.
P64: 7.  Downstream Inputs
P65: The following quantities established above are the source-term and length-scale inputs for the downstream Phase 1 case-setup, mesh-study, and reporting artifacts:
P66: •  Site design envelope: ambient 35–42 °C, RH 10–25 %, 20-ft wind 5–12 m/s (Section 2).
P67: •  Byram fireline intensity I = 10,040 kW/m (Section 3).
P68: •  Wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m (Section 3).
P69: •  LES sub-domain fire-front segment: 3.0 m (Section 5).
P70: •  Design fire heat release rate: 30.1 MW (Section 5.1).
P71: •  Plume characteristic diameter: D* = 3.76 m (Section 5.1).
P72: •  Froude ratio range across the site design envelope: ~0.9–2.2 (Section 4); regime classification and solver selection per Modeling Standard §§2–3 to be documented in the case setup record (Section 4).
P73: •  Wall through-thickness modeling treatment: to be selected and documented per Modeling Standard §6, accounting for the metallic tie thermal-bridge path identified in Section 6.
P74: The 3.0 m segment, 30.1 MW source, and D* = 3.76 m established per Section 5 above are the inputs the fine grid dx = 0.5 m recorded in the Meshing and case-build log is sized against.
P75: The 5–12 m/s design wind envelope carries forward into the wind-inlet boundary conditions of the six-case matrix, per the solver selection made in Section 4; the puffing frequency of 0.87 Hz predicted by the f = 1.5·D^(-1/2) correlation per CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §4 for this plume sets the writeInterval and end-time requirements for each transient run.

P1: Interim Client Summary — Structural Wind-Load Case
P3: 1. Purpose
P4: This DRAFT is the interim client summary of the ASCE 7-22 structural wind-load extraction called out under SOW Section 3.2, and covers the pressure rollup produced from the wall-probe extraction run on 10/09/2025. The scope is limited to the standalone structural wind-load case; the Section 3.1 wildfire matrix is handled separately and is not addressed here.
P5: Section 3.2 asks the firm to develop the code-basis wall pressures at the OAS-WUI-01 envelope for a discrete-wind-speed check independent of the wildfire matrix, and to report peak pressures on windward, side, and leeward faces at probe locations laid out in the case verification plan. The values summarized below are drawn directly from the interim probe extraction (interim_wall_pressures.csv, 10/09/2025) with no post-processing beyond the peak rollup.
P6: 2. Case Description
P7: Basis of loading: ASCE 7-22 (Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures).
P8: Site: Tucson, Arizona (Ocotillo pilot envelope, OAS-WUI-01_revC geometry of record).
P9: Basic wind speed, V: 96 mph (Risk Category II mapped value for the Tucson site).
P10: Exposure category: C (open terrain with scattered obstructions, consistent with the Avra Valley WUI setting).
P11: Risk category: II.
P12: Mean roof height, h: 6.4 m.
P13: Directionality and topography factors and the velocity-pressure exposure coefficient are applied per ASCE 7-22 Chapter 26 at the mean roof height; wall pressure coefficients on windward, side, and leeward faces are taken from Chapter 27 (directional procedure, enclosed low-rise building) at the site aspect ratio.
P14: The probe grid used for peak extraction consists of ten windward probes spanning the windward face, five probes on each side wall (north and south), and five probes on the leeward face. Probe elevations are 0.8 m, 3.2 m, and 5.6 m above grade. All probe values reported are peak (envelope) values from the interim extraction.
P15: 3. Results
P16: The table below reproduces the peak pressures from the interim extraction file exactly as recorded.
P17: Sign convention: positive pressures act inward on the wall face; negative pressures indicate suction (outward). Values are peaks across the interim probe set; the full per-probe listing is retained in interim_wall_pressures.csv.
P18: 4. Discussion
P19: Taken at face value, the pressures returned by the interim rollup are negligible relative to the structural design demand envelope typically associated with the framing of a 6.4 m mean-roof-height enclosed building at a 96 mph basic wind speed in Exposure C. A 12.4 Pa peak windward pressure is a very small fraction of the wall loads that would ordinarily drive sizing of tie, header, and out-of-plane bending checks for a printed-concrete assembly of this scale, and the corresponding side-wall and leeward suctions (−9.5 Pa and −6.1 Pa peak) are similarly small.
P20: On that basis the interim reading is that the ASCE 7-22 wall loading, taken as extracted, does not govern the OAS-WUI-01 envelope. Wildfire-driven radiative and convective loading (SOW Section 3.1) and the E119 fire-endurance envelope remain the controlling design considerations for the assembly. No structural remediation of the OAS-WUI-01_revC envelope is indicated by this interim result.
P21: The client should treat these figures as provisional pending peer review under the firm's QA workflow. P2 [Normal]: 'VALIDATION MEMORANDUM'
P3 [Normal]: 'E119 Companion Simulation — Ocotillo Double-Wythe Printed-Concrete Wall Assembly'
P4 [Normal]: ''
P5 [Heading 1]: '1. Purpose and straight answer'
P6 [Normal]: 'This memorandum supplies the validation record required for §7 of Phase 1 rev B. It uses the E119 companion run as it stands, RBFMT-25-0918, IWFPE-CERT-25-0374, Ocotillo’s 10/09/2025 amended burn data, and drawing OAS_wall_assembly_section.png. No new runs or tests are used; nothing outside this memorandum is changed.'
P7 [Normal]: 'The discrepancy is a resolved model error, not measurement scatter: |E| is larger than the combined uncertainty, and positive E means the model predicts more endurance than the certified test observed, which is unconservative in a rating context. No unqualified validation claim may be issued. The §7 stub cannot be completed as a validation; it can be completed only as the §5 rollup plus a documented finding and a rework plan. The 10/09/2025 request to describe the simulation as “validated against the certified test” is not supported by this record.'
P8 [Normal]: 'The §7 stub’s S = 131 min stands as the prediction; its implication of validation does not. Section 7 must be rewritten around the §5 rollup and the §7 comparisons. This memorandum does not substitute D, change the certified rating, or assert wildfire performance.'
P9 [Heading 1]: '2. Records relied on'
P10 [Normal]: 'Paths are from the file-server root. All records were on file as of 10/10/2025 and none was altered for this memorandum.'
P11 [Normal]: 'Table 2-1. Records relied on. Two records are missing and condition this memorandum (below).'
P12 [Normal]: 'Missing record (a): no companion-run case record. There is no case-setup record, mesh, solver log, or resolution study for the E119 companion run; the only artifact is the results CSV. S can be read but not audited to Procedure §3, and no run identifier exists. Filing the record and assigning an identifier are conditions of closing §7.'
P13 [Normal]: 'Missing record (b): no project-specific u_val tabulation. Procedure §4 requires a project-specific tabulation of u_num, u_inp, and u_exp in the project QA folder before u_val is published; none is on file. The u_val used here is the §4 class default: u_num = ±4 min, u_inp = ±6 min, u_exp = ±5 min, combined to ±8.77 min and reported as ±9 min. The tabulation must be filed before signature.'
P14 [Heading 1]: '3. S — simulation prediction and how the crossing was read'
P15 [Normal]: 'Governing criterion. ASTM E119 applies two thermal-transmission criteria, both measured as rises above initial ambient: the nine-thermocouple average rise of 139 °C and the single-point rise of 181 °C; the earlier governs (RBFMT-25-0918 §§1 and 5.3; Digest §1). In RBFMT-25-0918 the single-point criterion was reached first, at 118 min at TC-6 over a 3.8 mm tie course; the average criterion was reached at 163 min (§§3.2 and 5.1–5.3). The governing criterion is the single-point 181 °C rise; its certified time is 118 min.'
P16 [Normal]: 'Run basis. The companion file has 181 data rows at 1 min cadence, t = 0–180 min. The t = 0 row is 21.0 °C in all five columns. The header cross-walks T_unexposed_avg_C to the §5.1 nine-TC average criterion and T_unexposed_max_C to the §5.2 single-point criterion at the unexposed face over the tie course. T_tie_C is a simulation-internal tie temperature with no direct RBFMT-25-0918 thermocouple equivalent; it is not the single-point analog, and using it gives a spurious 101 min crossing (Appendix A).'
P17 [Normal]: 'Crossing times. The thresholds applied to the run are 139 °C + 21.0 °C = 160.0 °C absolute for the average criterion and 181 °C + 21.0 °C = 202.0 °C absolute for the single-point criterion. Linear interpolation between the two adjacent 1 min samples gives 130.9 min for the single-point criterion (reported 131 min) and 176.1 min for the average criterion (reported 176 min). Appendix A holds the arithmetic and the bracketing samples; the body reports the crossing times, not the samples. Applying 181 °C as an absolute temperature instead of a rise gives 117.6 min → 118 min; that is the wrong rule, and its coincidence with the test endurance must not be used.'
P18 [Normal]: 'S = 131 min. The §7 stub’s number stands; its framing does not. The companion run has no run identifier; it is cited to the results file and SHA-256 b69ae8dbeb876080e0a421fa94200b0ffe9fef6f1ef10d731b5411575918d678. Assigning an identifier in the case record is a condition of closing §7.'
P19 [Heading 1]: '4. D — experimental value adopted and disposition on Bianca’s figure'
P20 [Normal]: 'D = 118 min (RBFMT-25-0918 §5.3: single-point at 118 min at TC-6; average at 163 min; the report is the certified test of record for IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.1). D is taken without adjustment.'
P21 [Normal]: 'Bianca Rennert’s 129 min is not admissible as D. Ocotillo transmitted Validation/burn_data_original_vs_revised.csv with Ms. Rennert’s email of 10/09/2025 11:42, revising the single-point endurance from 118 min to 129 min on the basis of a post-test TC-6 calibration correction; the average remains 163 min. Procedure §6 requires all three of: (1) a reissued report RBFMT-25-0918-R1, signed by the laboratory’s authorized signatory, stating the reason for revision; (2) a calibration certificate covering TC-6, with a date and calibration-authority reference traceable to the correction; and (3) an explicit statement in the reissued report that the revised value supersedes the original for all downstream use. None of the three is on file.'
P22 [Normal]: 'The in-force calibration record. RBFMT-25-0918 §7 lists RBFMT-CAL-25-0812-TC covering TC-1 through TC-10, calibrated 2025-08-12, NIST-traceable, in force on the 09/24/2025 test date, and covering the full observed temperature range. On the record as it stands, TC-6 was covered by an in-force calibration certificate. A client-side post-test correction is not a laboratory revision (Procedure §6). The transmittal is recorded in the correspondence folder, and D remains 118 min.'
P23 [Normal]: 'Scale check and materiality. At the crossing the run’s maximum is rising at about 1.6 °C/min (200.5 °C at 130 min to 202.1 °C at 131 min), so an 11 min shift corresponds to roughly 18 °C of TC-6 correction — a large instrument correction that no certificate on file supports. At D = 129 min the rollup would read E = 131 min − 129 min = +2 min against a criterion of 12.9 min, and |E| = 2 min would sit inside u_val = 8.77 min; the numerical tests would be met. The 129 min also sits just below the 129.8 min clearing bound for the certified D. That is why Procedure §6 exists; it is not a reason to use 129 min.'
P24 [Heading 1]: '5. Rollup, criterion, uncertainty, and the clearing bound'
P25 [Normal]: 'This is the rollup the reviewer must be able to sign. It is in the Procedure §3 order, every value carries its unit, and limits are stated as they fall.'
P26 [Normal]: 'Table 5-1. Validation rollup of record. |E| = 13 min exceeds both the 11.8 min criterion and the ±8.77 min validation uncertainty.'
P27 [Normal]: 'Procedure §5 disposition. Because |E| exceeds both the criterion and u_val, the deliverable may not be released with an unqualified validation claim. This memorandum records a documented finding and calls for model rework; the remedy is not a substitution of D (Procedure §§6 and 8). The primary test fails by 1.2 min against 11.8 min; the secondary fails by 4.23 min against 8.77 min, or by 4 min against the reported ±9 min. Even if the criterion were rounded to 12 min, |E| = 13 min would still exceed it by 1 min.'
P28 [Heading 1]: '6. Geometry — is the assembly in the run the one the certification covers?'
P29 [Normal]: 'Answer: yes, on every parameter the certification tabulates. IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.2 tabulates nine parameters; the run geometry, OAS-WUI-01_revC, conforms on all nine.'
P30 [Normal]: 'Table 6-1. Certified geometry against run geometry (IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.2). The first nine rows are the certification’s tabulated parameters; the tenth is an idealization, not a certified parameter.'
P31 [Normal]: 'What that rests on. (1) The results-file header names OAS-WUI-01_revC and cross-walks its columns to RBFMT-25-0918 §5.1 and §5.2. (2) The revC property table carries the nine values above; revC is the geometry of record in SOW §2 and the deliverable manifest. (3) The snappyHexMesh log names OAS-WUI-01_revC.FCStd, records an export timestamp of 2025-10-08 16:42:11 -0700 (received with the signed SOW), and records a mesh build on 10/09/2025 from 07:14 to 10:26 MST. (4) revD was received on 10/09/2025 at 16:12, after the mesh build; it is not the geometry in the run. (5) The dimensioned drawing OAS_wall_assembly_section.png carries drawing ID OAS-WA-305mm-DW and is identified as the same assembly in scoping memo §6 and Phase 1 rev B §3.5.'
P32 [Normal]: 'Two qualifications. First, panel plan size is not a certified parameter: the tested specimen was 3.05 m × 3.05 m and the model panel is 1830 mm × 2745 mm, so conformance rests on the layup and tie schedule, not on panel dimensions. The difference is a geometric idealization and belongs in u_inp. Second, revD is not covered: its 610 mm parapet, 3355 mm total height, 50 mm coping, and 25 mm drip overhang are deviations from the tabulated geometry and fall outside IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.2. revD is not in the run; it is a geometry revision superseding the geometry of record, and SOW §8 requires an executed change order before any work on it. No such change order is on file. The certification is also limited to the §1.3 conditions: non-load-bearing, standard E119 curve, no applied load, no hose-stream retest (Ironwood §§5.3–5.4).'
P33 [Heading 1]: '7. The two comparisons, what they say, and the rework'
P34 [Normal]: 'The two requested comparisons are the separation between the criteria in the test against the same separation in the run, and the distance from the governing point to the nine-point mean at governance in each.'
P35 [Normal]: 'Table 7-1. The two diagnostic comparisons. Times are to the nearest minute; the unrounded separation is shown once.'
P36 [Normal]: 'What they say. The separation is preserved to 0.2 min (0.4 %), and the model’s tie hot-spot excess is slightly larger than the test’s (+6.2 °C, +7 %). The model captures which criterion governs, why it governs, and in what order; the tie-bridge single-point mechanism is not mis-modelled and the tie path is not under-represented. Both criteria are late by the same 13 min. A near-pure translation in time points to a uniform bias in the whole-assembly thermal response or in the imposed exposure, not a local mechanism error. It is not a reason to adjust D.'
P37 [Normal]: 'Where the rework belongs. In the companion model, not in D and not in the wildfire matrix. First, a documented case-setup record and u_num evidence must be created; neither exists today. Then, per Modeling Standard rev 4: a multi-region CHT treatment with each tie a separate solid region and refinement zones at every tie–concrete interface at least a factor of four finer than the bulk leaf mesh (§6); temperature-dependent k, ρ, and cp for solids (§3.5); cavity radiation by fvDOM with concrete and steel emissivities of 0.90 and 0.25 (dimensionless; App. A); and a furnace-side exposure audit against the E119 gas-temperature history actually delivered (Digest §1). Without the case record the 13 min cannot be attributed further; the diagnostics do not support a local tie-mechanism error and point instead to the bulk thermal response or the exposure.'
P38 [Normal]: 'Has it started? No. No setup file, mesh, solver log, verification study, or rework note for the companion run exists on file. CO-001 (marketing animation, 12 h, $2,400) and CO-002 (mesh refinement on wildfire cases 240°/8 m/s and 270°/8 m/s, 30 h, $6,750) were executed 10/09/2025, but neither touches the companion model. The budget shows the reviewer commission ($4,225) and contingency ($8,000) unspent and HPC actual at $2,100 of $6,200. The only October solve on file is attempt 3 of the wildfire model (6 h 41 min wall clock, 64 cores, 424.3 CPU-hours), not the companion and itself nonconforming (§10). The Q3 cluster export ends 09/30/2025 with no CFDME-2025-041 jobs; it neither evidences nor excludes October compute.'
P39 [Heading 1]: '8. What this establishes about the wildfire claim, and what would close the gap'
P40 [Normal]: 'What the exercise establishes. At most, the comparison supports a mechanistic reading of E119 thermal-transmission behaviour: the single-point criterion governs, the two criteria are separated by 45 min in both the test and the run, and the tie hot-spot is present and slightly larger in the model. That is useful model-diagnostic information. It is not a validation: the numerical tests in §5 are not met even for E119, and S comes from a run with no documented case record.'
P41 [Normal]: 'What it does not establish. It does not establish wildfire performance, wildfire survival time, or the marketing proposition that the assembly is “more fire-resistant than wood-frame construction in a Sonoran WUI wildfire.” There is no wildfire-exposure physical test on the project, no wood-frame comparator test, and no certified D for a wildfire exposure. ASTM E119 is a comparative assembly rating under the standard furnace curve, not a WUI exposure (Procedure §7; Digest §4; Ironwood §5.2; SOW §7). The finding does not extend to any layup other than revC, to loaded configurations, or to hose-stream criteria (Ironwood §§5.3–5.4).'
P42 [Normal]: 'What would close the gap. Three things: (i) one or more certified third-party wildfire-exposure tests of the same assembly, with wind-driven radiant and convective exposure and measured incident heat flux, gas temperature, and unexposed-face and tie temperatures at the same instrument locations; if the claim remains comparative, a paired wood-frame specimen tested in the same campaign; (ii) a companion wildfire CFD run in that configuration; and (iii) a validation under Procedure rev 2 using D from that certified report. Anything less leaves the claim as a proposition, not a validated result.'
P43 [Normal]: 'Required reporting form for any future comparison. Report S, D, E, and u_val, in that order, in a single line or table, each with its unit, citing the run identifier and the certified report number and clause. Then state the criterion (10 % of D) and both secondary comparisons: |E| against u_val, and the sign of E against the physical expectation. Never a yes/no; never “matches,” “agrees,” “confirms,” “is validated,” or “within tolerance” in place of the numbers (Procedure §3; Digest §2). The u_val build must be project-specific: u_num from an LES resolution study meeting D*/dx in the 5–10 band (dimensionless) and Pope resolved-TKE ≥ 80 % (Verification Standard rev 3 §5), u_inp from fuel, boundary-condition, and geometry uncertainty, and u_exp from the wildfire test instrumentation. A compliant line reads: “S = ___ min; D = ___ min; E = ___ min; u_val = ___ min (u_num ___ min, u_inp ___ min, u_exp ___ min); criterion = ___ min (10 % of D); |E| vs criterion ___; |E| vs u_val ___; sign ___.”'
P44 [Heading 1]: '9. Bianca’s figure and the certified rating'
P45 [Normal]: 'If the 129 min were ever substantiated by a reissued RBFMT-25-0918-R1 with a TC-6 calibration certificate and an explicit supersession statement, the governing single-point endurance would move to 129 min. That clears the 120 min 2-hour rung by 9 min; the current certified 118 min falls 2 min short (Ironwood §3). It would therefore support a 2-hour fire-resistance rating on the same non-load-bearing, no-hose-stream basis. It would also change this rollup to E = 131 min − 129 min = +2 min against a criterion of 12.9 min, with |E| = 2 min inside u_val = 8.77 min; the numerical tests would be met. A D of 129 min leaves only 0.8 min of margin below the 129.8 min prediction that would clear the criterion against the certified D; that sensitivity is why Procedure §6 exists, not a reason to depart from it.'
P46 [Normal]: 'Who may act. Only Red Butte can reissue the report, and only Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering — Marla Kettering, PE, AZ PE #45106 — can certify or restate the rating. Ironwood §4 is explicit: “No other party may certify or restate this rating.” The CFD ME is not entitled to act: a validation finding is not a rating action (Procedure §9), and the SOW excludes any determination of ratings, listings, or certifications (SOW §§1, 8, and 10). Ocotillo marketing may not restate the rating either. This memorandum records Ocotillo’s request and the admissibility test; it makes no request of Red Butte or Ironwood and takes no position on the rating. Stamp language (verbatim): “CFD thermal analysis only. Fire-resistance rating certified separately by others.”'
P47 [Heading 1]: '10. What this means for the rest of Phase 1'
P48 [List Number]: 'Phase 1 rev B §7 and §8. Section 7 can be closed only as a documented finding, not as a validation. Section 8 conclusions cannot use “validated.” Phase 1 rev B cannot be issued for client transmission on the current record.'
P49 [List Number]: 'The six-case wildfire matrix is not conforming as set up. The only filed case-setup record is the DWA aerospace template: steady rhoSimpleFoam, k-omega SST RANS, no combustion, no radiation, adiabatic walls, no conjugate regions, and aerospace reference conditions of 26,500 Pa, 223 K, and 0.4 kg/m³. Attempt 3 partially rebuilt to fireFoam with EDC and fvDOM, but runs the fire solver in a forced steady SIMPLE loop (a single outer corrector, nOuterCorrectors = 1), with k-epsilon RANS and time interpreted as iteration count; the live controlDict still has adjustTimeStep no, endTime 2000 (iteration count), and writeControl timeStep, and the run stalled in a limit cycle. That record, taken as a whole, does not conform to Modeling Standard rev 4 §§3.1–3.6, 4, 5, 6, and 7. The matrix must be rebuilt before the 10/20/2025 LES setup memo and 11/07/2025 delivery; this is the dominant schedule risk, ahead of the companion rework.'
P50 [List Number]: '270° is not new scope. The signed SOW §3.1 matrix already contains 270° at 5, 8, and 12 m/s as cases 3.1-D, 3.1-E, and 3.1-F. The 10/09/2025 request for a “second direction” does not require a change order; SOW §8 makes only directions beyond 240° and 270° out of scope. The change-order discussion should be corrected on that point.'
P51 [List Number]: 'revD must not be picked up. It requires (a) an executed change order under SOW §8 and (b) recognition that it is outside IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 and would need a new test and a new certification before any rating statement.'
P52 [List Number]: 'The 10/27/2025 Red Butte window is a confirmatory ASTM E119 test (SOW §5), not a wildfire-phase physical test. Phase 1 rev B §4.2 and the staffing assignment “Red Butte confirmatory ASTM E119 test for Ocotillo Phase 1 wildfire assembly” misdescribe it. At most it supplies a second independent E119 dataset for a repeat comparison.'
P53 [List Number]: 'Independent structural wind-load defect. The interim summary reports 12.4 Pa windward, but the wind-load basis memo §4 computes 12.4 psf = 594 Pa (Units SOP §3); this unit-carry defect keeps checklist item 9 open and must be corrected before issue.'
P54 [List Number]: 'Launch timing. It is a commercial constraint and cannot move a validation outcome; no number or claim goes into the press deck until the rework is complete and re-reported.'

P56 [Normal]: 'Table 11-1. The memo closes item 6 only.'

E119 Companion Simulation — Ocotillo Double-Wythe Printed-Concrete Wall Assembly
1.
This memorandum supplies the validation record required for §7 of Phase 1 rev B.
It uses the E119 companion run as it stands, RBFMT-25-0918, IWFPE-CERT-25-0374, Ocotillo’s 10/09/2025 amended burn data, and drawing OAS_wall_assembly_section.png.
The §7 stub cannot be completed as a validation; it can be completed only as the §5 rollup plus a documented finding and a rework plan.
The 10/09/2025 request to describe the simulation as “validated against the certified test” is not supported by this record.
The §7 stub’s S = 131 min stands as the prediction; its implication of validation does not.
Section 7 must be rewritten around the §5 rollup and the §7 comparisons.
2.
All records were on file as of 10/10/2025 and none was altered for this memorandum.
Table 2-1.
There is no case-setup record, mesh, solver log, or resolution study for the E119 companion run; the only artifact is the results CSV.
S can be read but not audited to Procedure §3, and no run identifier exists.
Filing the record and assigning an identifier are conditions of closing §7.
Procedure §4 requires a project-specific tabulation of u_num, u_inp, and u_exp in the project QA folder before u_val is published; none is on file.
The u_val used here is the §4 class default: u_num = ±4 min, u_inp = ±6 min, u_exp = ±5 min, combined to ±8.77 min and reported as ±9 min.
3.
ASTM E119 applies two thermal-transmission criteria, both measured as rises above initial ambient: the nine-thermocouple average rise of 139 °C and the single-point rise of 181 °C; the earlier governs (RBFMT-25-0918 §§1 and 5.3; Digest §1).
In RBFMT-25-0918 the single-point criterion was reached first, at 118 min at TC-6 over a 3.8 mm tie course; the average criterion was reached at 163 min (§§3.2 and 5.1–5.3).
The governing criterion is the single-point 181 °C rise; its certified time is 118 min.
The companion file has 181 data rows at 1 min cadence, t = 0–180 min.
The t = 0 row is 21.0 °C in all five columns.
The header cross-walks T_unexposed_avg_C to the §5.1 nine-TC average criterion and T_unexposed_max_C to the §5.2 single-point criterion at the unexposed face over the tie course.
T_tie_C is a simulation-internal tie temperature with no direct RBFMT-25-0918 thermocouple equivalent; it is not the single-point analog, and using it gives a spurious 101 min crossing (Appendix A).
The thresholds applied to the run are 139 °C + 21.0 °C = 160.0 °C absolute for the average criterion and 181 °C + 21.0 °C = 202.0 °C absolute for the single-point criterion.
Linear interpolation between the two adjacent 1 min samples gives 130.9 min for the single-point criterion (reported 131 min) and 176.1 min for the average criterion (reported 176 min).
Applying 181 °C as an absolute temperature instead of a rise gives 117.6 min → 118 min; that is the wrong rule, and its coincidence with the test endurance must not be used.
S = 131 min.
The §7 stub’s number stands; its framing does not.
The companion run has no run identifier; it is cited to the results file and SHA-256 b69ae8dbeb876080e0a421fa94200b0ffe9fef6f1ef10d731b5411575918d678.
Assigning an identifier in the case record is a condition of closing §7.
4.
D = 118 min (RBFMT-25-0918 §5.3: single-point at 118 min at TC-6; average at 163 min; the report is the certified test of record for IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.1).
Bianca Rennert’s 129 min is not admissible as D.
Rennert’s email of 10/09/2025 11:42, revising the single-point endurance from 118 min to 129 min on the basis of a post-test TC-6 calibration correction; the average remains 163 min.
Procedure §6 requires all three of: (1) a reissued report RBFMT-25-0918-R1, signed by the laboratory’s authorized signatory, stating the reason for revision; (2) a calibration certificate covering TC-6, with a date and calibration-authority reference traceable to the correction; and (3) an explicit statement in the reissued report that the revised value supersedes the original for all downstream use.
RBFMT-25-0918 §7 lists RBFMT-CAL-25-0812-TC covering TC-1 through TC-10, calibrated 2025-08-12, NIST-traceable, in force on the 09/24/2025 test date, and covering the full observed temperature range.
On the record as it stands, TC-6 was covered by an in-force calibration certificate.
A client-side post-test correction is not a laboratory revision (Procedure §6).
The transmittal is recorded in the correspondence folder, and D remains 118 min.
At the crossing the run’s maximum is rising at about 1.6 °C/min (200.5 °C at 130 min to 202.1 °C at 131 min), so an 11 min shift corresponds to roughly 18 °C of TC-6 correction — a large instrument correction that no certificate on file supports.
At D = 129 min the rollup would read E = 131 min − 129 min = +2 min against a criterion of 12.9 min, and |E| = 2 min would sit inside u_val = 8.77 min; the numerical tests would be met.
The 129 min also sits just below the 129.8 min clearing bound for the certified D.
That is why Procedure §6 exists; it is not a reason to use 129 min.

It is in the Procedure §3 order, every value carries its unit, and limits are stated as they fall.

|E| = 13 min exceeds both the 11.8 min criterion and the ±8.77 min validation uncertainty.
Procedure §5 disposition.
This memorandum records a documented finding and calls for model rework; the remedy is not a substitution of D (Procedure §§6 and 8).
The primary test fails by 1.2 min against 11.8 min; the secondary fails by 4.23 min against 8.77 min, or by 4 min against the reported ±9 min.
Even if the criterion were rounded to 12 min, |E| = 13 min would still exceed it by 1 min.

Table 6-1.
Certified geometry against run geometry (IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.2).
(1) The results-file header names OAS-WUI-01_revC and cross-walks its columns to RBFMT-25-0918 §5.1 and §5.2.
(2) The revC property table carries the nine values above; revC is the geometry of record in SOW §2 and the deliverable manifest.

Both criteria are late by the same 13 min.

A); and a furnace-side exposure audit against the E119 gas-temperature history actually delivered (Digest §1).
Without the case record the 13 min cannot be attributed further; the diagnostics do not support a local tie-mechanism error and point instead to the bulk thermal response or the exposure.
CO-001 (marketing animation, 12 h, $2,400) and CO-002 (mesh refinement on wildfire cases 240°/8 m/s and 270°/8 m/s, 30 h, $6,750) were executed 10/09/2025, but neither touches the companion model.

The Q3 cluster export ends 09/30/2025 with no CFDME-2025-041 jobs; it neither evidences nor excludes October compute.
8.
At most, the comparison supports a mechanistic reading of E119 thermal-transmission behaviour: the single-point criterion governs, the two criteria are separated by 45 min in both the test and the run, and the tie hot-spot is present and slightly larger in the model.
It is not a validation: the numerical tests in §5 are not met even for E119, and S comes from a run with no documented case record.
ASTM E119 is a comparative assembly rating under the standard furnace curve, not a WUI exposure (Procedure §7; Digest §4; Ironwood §5.2; SOW §7).
The finding does not extend to any layup other than revC, to loaded configurations, or to hose-stream criteria (Ironwood §§5.3–5.4).
Three things: (i) one or more certified third-party wildfire-exposure tests of the same assembly, with wind-driven radiant and convective exposure and measured incident heat flux, gas temperature, and unexposed-face and tie temperatures at the same instrument locations; if the claim remains comparative, a paired wood-frame specimen tested in the same campaign; (ii) a companion wildfire CFD run in that configuration; and (iii) a validation under Procedure rev 2 using D from that certified report.
Then state the criterion (10 % of D) and both secondary comparisons: |E| against u_val, and the sign of E against the physical expectation.
Never a yes/no; never “matches,” “agrees,” “confirms,” “is validated,” or “within tolerance” in place of the numbers (Procedure §3; Digest §2).
The u_val build must be project-specific: u_num from an LES resolution study meeting D*/dx in the 5–10 band (dimensionless) and Pope resolved-TKE ≥ 80 % (Verification Standard rev 3 §5), u_inp from fuel, boundary-condition, and geometry uncertainty, and u_exp from the wildfire test instrumentation.
A compliant line reads: “S = ___ min; D = ___ min; E = ___ min; u_val = ___ min (u_num ___ min, u_inp ___ min, u_exp ___ min); criterion = ___ min (10 % of D); |E| vs criterion ___; |E| vs u_val ___; sign ___.”

If the 129 min were ever substantiated by a reissued RBFMT-25-0918-R1 with a TC-6 calibration certificate and an explicit supersession statement, the governing single-point endurance would move to 129 min.
That clears the 120 min 2-hour rung by 9 min; the current certified 118 min falls 2 min short (Ironwood §3).

A D of 129 min leaves only 0.8 min of margin below the 129.8 min prediction that would clear the criterion against the certified D; that sensitivity is why Procedure §6 exists, not a reason to depart from it.
Only Red Butte can reissue the report, and only Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering — Marla Kettering, PE, AZ PE #45106 — can certify or restate the rating.
Ironwood §4 is explicit: “No other party may certify or restate this rating.” The CFD ME is not entitled to act: a validation finding is not a rating action (Procedure §9), and the SOW excludes any determination of ratings, listings, or certifications (SOW §§1, 8, and 10).

157 Bianca — the E119 companion run does not validate. It predicts S = 131 min against the certified D = 118 min, so the model error is E = +13 min; that exceeds both the firm’s 11.8 min acceptance criterion (10 % of D) and the ±9 min validation uncertainty. I understand the 129 min figure, but it cannot be used: there is no reissued Red Butte report RBFMT-25-0918-R1, no TC-6 calibration certificate supporting the correction, and no supersession statement. 7 The discrepancy is a resolved model error, not measurement scatter: |E| is larger than the combined uncertainty, and positive E means the model predicts more endurance than the certified test observed, which is unconservative in a rating context. No unqualified validation claim may be issued. The §7 stub cannot be completed as a validation; it can be completed only as the §5 rollup plus a documented finding and a rework plan. The 10/09/2025 request to describe the simulation as “validated against the certified test” is not supported by this record.
42 What would close the gap. Three things: (i) one or more certified third-party wildfire-exposure tests of the same assembly, with wind-driven radiant and convective exposure and measured incident heat flux, gas temperature, and unexposed-face and tie temperatures at the same instrument locations; if the claim remains comparative, a paired wood-frame specimen tested in the same campaign; (ii) a companion wildfire CFD run in that configuration; and (iii) a validation under Procedure rev 2 using D from that certified report. Anything less leaves the claim as a proposition, not a validated result.
43 Required reporting form for any future comparison. Report S, D, E, and u_val, in that order, in a single line or table, each with its unit, citing the run identifier and the certified report number and clause. Then state the criterion (10 % of D) and both secondary comparisons: |E| against u_val, and the sign of E against the physical expectation. Never a yes/no; never “matches,” “agrees,” “confirms,” “is validated,” or “within tolerance” in place of the numbers (Procedure §3; Digest §2). The u_val build must be project-specific: u_num from an LES resolution study meeting D*/dx in the 5–10 band (dimensionless) and Pope resolved-TKE ≥ 80 % (Verification Standard rev 3 §5), u_inp from fuel, boundary-condition, and geometry uncertainty, and u_exp from the wildfire test instrumentation. A compliant line reads: “S = ___ min; D = ___ min; E = ___ min; u_val = ___ min (u_num ___ min, u_inp ___ min, u_exp ___ min); criterion = ___ min (10 % of D); |E| vs criterion ___; |E| vs u_val ___; sign ___.”

=================== Firm/QA/CFDME_Validation_Procedure_rev2.pdf
           THE CFD ME | Tucson, Arizona | Validation QA Procedure — ASME V&V 20 | rev 2 | Effective 05/01/2025


Document: CFDME-QA-VAL-002 Author: Marguerite Falk, PE — Technical Director & Reviewing Engineer (AZ PE
#42798) Supersedes: CFDME-QA-VAL-001 (rev 1, Effective 03/01/2024) Approved: Gordon Selby, PE — Owner &
Principal Engineer (AZ PE #48213)


1. Purpose and Scope
This procedure governs how validation is performed, evaluated, and reported for every deliverable of The CFD
Mechanical Engineer, LLC ("The CFD ME") that carries a validation claim. A validation claim is any statement,
quantitative or qualitative, that a simulation prediction reproduces a physical measurement within a stated tolerance.
Whenever such a claim is made — in a client report, a peer-review response, a testimony exhibit, or an internal
working record — the reasoning, arithmetic, and acceptance decision shall follow the steps set out here.
The scope covers all CFD analyses executed by staff engineers, remote engineers, and contracted vendors of the
firm, regardless of solver stack, regime, or client. It applies from the moment a validation reference is selected for a
project until the corresponding project file is closed and archived. Deviation from this procedure requires a written
waiver signed by both the reviewing engineer of record and the firm's owner, filed to the project's QA folder before the
deliverable is issued.
The procedure does not certify third-party test data, nor does it substitute for the engineering judgment of the
professional engineer of record. It fixes the form in which validation is expressed and the criterion against which it is
judged; it does not relieve any engineer of independent responsibility for the underlying analysis.

2. References
The following external standards inform this procedure. The firm holds single-user licenses to each; proprietary text is
not reproduced. The provisions relied upon are restated below in the firm's own words with citations back to the
source clause.
• ASME V&V 20-2009 (R2016), Standard for Verification and Validation in Computational Fluid Dynamics
   and Heat Transfer. Framework for expressing validation as a comparison error with an associated validation
   uncertainty. See ASME V&V 20 Section 1 (validation framework and definitions) for the source
   formulation restated in Section 3 below, and Section 5 for the components combined in Section 4 below.
• ASTM E119-24, Standard Test Methods for Fire Tests of Building Construction and Materials. Referenced
   for the exposure curve and the two thermal-transmission end-point criteria applied by testing laboratories. See
   ASTM E119 Section 8 (thermal transmission on the unexposed face · average rise and single-point) for the
   criteria whose interpretation is restated in Section 7.
• NIST NCSTAR 1-5 series, Fire Investigation of the World Trade Center Disaster, thermal-model validation
   appendices. Cited for community practice on uncertainty accounting in conjugate fire-thermal problems; not
   binding.
• Internal: CFD Modeling Standards - Fire & Buoyant Flows (M. Falk, PE); QA Verification Standard -
   Mesh & Resolution (M. Falk, PE); External Standards Digest (M. Falk, PE).

3. Model-Error Formulation
Validation shall be reported as the model error E = S - D with its validation uncertainty u_val, and never as a yes/no.
• S is the simulation prediction — the value produced by the CFD run using the model, mesh, solver, boundary
   conditions, and material properties documented in the report.
• D is the certified experimental value — the corresponding measurement produced by the physical test of record,
   drawn from the certified third-party report described in Section 6.
• E carries a sign. A positive E denotes a simulation that predicts more of the measured quantity than the test
   observed; a negative E, less. The sign is retained through every downstream comparison and is required in every
   rollup.
The equation E = S - D is the reporting form. Every deliverable that carries a validation claim shall present S, D, E,
and u_val in a single line or table, in that order, with a citation to the physical test report from which D is taken and to
 the run identifier from which S is taken. Descriptive words such as "matches," "agrees," "confirms," or "is validated"
are inadmissible substitutes for the numerical statement. The reviewing engineer shall reject any submitted
deliverable that omits any of the four quantities or that replaces the numerical rollup with a qualitative
characterization.
The requirement to report E with u_val — rather than a binary outcome — is not a matter of firm style. A yes/no
verdict conceals the sign and magnitude of the discrepancy, hides whether the disagreement is within measurement
scatter or resolved as a model error, and forecloses the diagnostic reasoning the validation exercise exists to support.
The reviewing engineer shall enforce the reporting form on every deliverable.

4. Uncertainty Build-Up
The validation uncertainty u_val is the root-sum-square (RSS) combination of three independent components, each
expressed in the units of the quantity being validated:
1. Numerical uncertainty, u_num. Reflects discretization, iterative convergence, and round-off contributions in S.
For the class of problem addressed in Section 8 — a conjugate thermal simulation of a compartment-wall assembly
under an ASTM E119 exposure — the firm's default value is ±4 min, established from prior three-grid conjugate
thermal studies on similar assemblies. A project-specific value shall be substituted where a resolution study or
convergence study supports one. 2. Input uncertainty, u_inp. Reflects propagation of uncertainties in material
properties (temperature-dependent conductivity, density, specific heat), boundary conditions (furnace-side
temperature histories, ambient side convective and radiative loss), and geometric idealization (leaf thickness, tie
diameter and spacing, cavity dimension). The firm's default value for the same class of problem is ±6 min. 3.
Experimental uncertainty, u_exp. Reflects instrument, calibration, and placement contributions to D as reported by
the testing laboratory. For calibrated Type-K thermocouples of the class used in ASTM E119 furnace work, the firm's
default value is ±5 min.
Combining by root-sum-square:
  u_val = sqrt( u_num^2 + u_inp^2 + u_exp^2 )
  = sqrt( 4^2 + 6^2 + 5^2 )
  = sqrt( 16 + 36 + 25 )
  = sqrt( 77 )
  = ±8.77 min
The result is reported to whole minutes: u_val = ±9 min for this class of problem.
Two guardrails apply.
First, the three components must be independent. If the numerical model uses lab-measured material properties
whose uncertainty is already folded into D, that property uncertainty shall not be double-counted in u_inp. The
reviewing engineer shall verify independence at the peer review stage.
Second, the default values shall be reviewed at least annually or whenever a project uses a materially different
assembly, exposure, or instrument class. A project-specific tabulation of u_num, u_inp, u_exp shall be recorded in
the project QA folder before u_val is published.

5. Acceptance Criterion
The firm acceptance criterion is |E| ≤ 10% of D.
The criterion is scaled: it grows with the endurance value being validated, so short endurances demand tighter
agreement in absolute minutes and long endurances tolerate more. A 30-minute endurance carries a 3-minute band;
a 120-minute endurance carries a 12-minute band; a 240-minute endurance carries a 24-minute band. This scaling is
deliberate. Absolute-minute criteria are unstable across the range of assemblies the firm analyzes; a 5-minute
absolute tolerance is loose against a 30-minute rating and severe against a 4-hour rating. A percentage-of-D criterion
is stable across the range and disciplines short-endurance work where the absolute stakes are largest.
Two secondary tests accompany the primary criterion and shall appear in every validation rollup:
• Compare |E| to u_val. If |E| ≤ u_val, the discrepancy is within the combined validation uncertainty and is best
   characterized as measurement-plus-model scatter. If |E| > u_val, the discrepancy is resolved as a model error —
   larger than the noise floor of the exercise — and shall be treated as an actionable finding, regardless of whether
    the primary 10% criterion is met.
• Compare the sign of E to the direction of the physical expectation. A simulation that consistently over-predicts
   endurance carries different engineering implications from one that consistently under-predicts; the sign is
   preserved in every rollup and discussed in the report narrative.
A deliverable in which |E| exceeds the criterion, or in which |E| exceeds u_val, or both, shall not be released with an
unqualified validation claim. The reviewing engineer determines whether the deliverable may be released with a
documented finding, whether the model shall be reworked, or whether the validation reference itself is unsuitable and
a different reference shall be sought.

6. Source of D
D shall be taken from the certified third-party test report of record. Client-amended values may not be
substituted for D absent a reissued report from the testing laboratory of record and a calibration certificate authorizing
the revision. Post-test amendments transmitted by the client but not authorized by the lab are not admissible as D.
The rule is strict for a reason. D is the physical anchor of the validation; if D moves for any reason other than a
documented laboratory action, the validation ceases to be against the physical test and becomes a comparison
against a preferred number. The two states are indistinguishable in the report if the substitution is silent, and the
record of the exercise is corrupted.
The following forms of documentation are required to substitute a revised D:
1. A reissued report from the testing laboratory of record, bearing the same report number as the original with an
amendment sequence (e.g., "-R1"), signed by the laboratory's authorized signatory, and stating the reason for the
revision. 2. A calibration certificate covering the instrument or measurement whose revision is at issue, with a date
and calibration-authority reference sufficient to trace the correction. 3. An explicit statement, in the reissued report,
that the revised value supersedes the value in the original report for all downstream use.
Absent any of the three, the original value stands. The reviewing engineer shall reject any deliverable that draws D
from a client-amended figure not backed by the above documentation. A polite, specific, thermocouple-calibration
explanation transmitted by a client is not a laboratory revision; the analyst shall record the client transmittal in the
correspondence folder and continue to use the certified D. Any pressure to depart from this rule — from schedule,
from commercial positioning, or from a persuasive account of what "really" happened at the test — shall be resolved
by returning to the reissued-report requirement.

7. Scope Limitation
ASTM E119 exposes an assembly to the standard building time-temperature curve, which is not a WUI
wildfire exposure. E119 endurance is therefore a comparative assembly rating, not a prediction of wildfire survival
time. Validation against E119 data validates the model against E119; it does not validate a wildfire performance
claim.
The distinction is not a formality. The E119 curve is a smooth, monotonically rising fuel-continuous compartment fire
scenario intended to grade the relative thermal performance of building assemblies under a repeatable exposure. A
wildland-urban interface exposure is a wind-driven, radiation-dominated, transient fire-front event whose peak heat
flux, duration, and spatial distribution differ from E119 at every axis. An assembly with a two-hour E119 rating is not
thereby a two-hour wildfire assembly, and no algebraic manipulation of an E119 result yields a wildfire survival time.
Firm practice on this point:
• Reports that use E119 test data to validate a CFD model shall state, in the validation section, that the validation
   exercise establishes model fidelity against the E119 exposure and shall not extrapolate that finding to wildfire,
   hydrocarbon-pool, or other non-E119 exposures.
• Where a project's ultimate objective is a wildfire performance claim, the validation section shall separately identify
   (i) what E119 data validates, (ii) what it does not, and (iii) what additional physical evidence would be required to
   close the gap.
• Marketing or commercial statements that translate an E119 rating into a wildfire performance figure are outside
   the firm's stamp and shall not appear in any firm-issued deliverable.

8. Worked Example — Illustrative Assembly
 The worked example below illustrates the arithmetic of Sections 3 through 5 using a hypothetical compartment-wall
assembly. The values used are illustrative and are not the values of record for any live project; they are pedagogic
only.
Inputs (illustrative).
• D = 120 min. Certified single-point endurance drawn from a hypothetical laboratory ASTM E119 report for the
   illustrative assembly. The single-point criterion governs per ASTM E119.
• S = 126 min. Simulation prediction from a conjugate CFD run mirroring the E119 furnace exposure for the same
   illustrative assembly.
• u_val = ±9 min. Per Section 4, using default values (u_num = ±4, u_inp = ±6, u_exp = ±5), combined by
   root-sum-square.
Rollup (illustrative).
• E = S − D = 126 − 120 = +6 min. Reported as E = +6 min, sign retained.
• Primary criterion: 0.10 × D = 0.10 × 120 = 12 min. Comparison: |E| = 6 min ≤ 12 min. The primary criterion is
   met.
• Secondary comparison to u_val: |E| = 6 min ≤ 9 min. The discrepancy is within the combined validation
   uncertainty.
Conclusion (illustrative). |E| = 6 min ≤ 12 min criterion AND ≤ 9 min u_val. The illustrative simulation would validate
against the illustrative certified test under the primary criterion, with the discrepancy sitting within the combined
validation uncertainty.
The point of the worked example is the arithmetic and the reporting form, not the outcome. In practice the analyst
reads D from the certified third-party report per Section 6, computes S from the run of record, tabulates u_val per
Section 4, and applies Section 5 to arrive at an acceptance decision. The engineering action that follows from a
non-validating rollup — grid resolution review, boundary-condition audit, material-property review, geometric
idealization audit — is not a substitution of D. Section 6 governs D.

9. Stamp Boundary
The CFD analyst of record stamps CFD thermal analysis only. The firm's stamp block on any deliverable that carries
a validation claim under this procedure shall read:
"CFD thermal analysis only. Fire-resistance rating certified separately by others."
Fire-resistance rating certification is reserved to the fire-protection professional engineer of record for the project.
Where the firm's CFD work supports a rating certification issued by a fire-protection PE, the firm's deliverable and the
fire-protection PE's certification remain separately stamped and separately scoped. A CFD validation finding under
this procedure is not a rating action; a rating action is not a CFD validation finding. Neither substitutes for the other,
and neither shall be represented as the other in any client-facing communication.

The evaluation reported here was performed in accordance with ASTM E119, Standard Test Methods for Fire Tests
