3. Conversions in Routine Use
The following conversions arise routinely in this office's work — ASCE 7-22 wind-load extraction, ASHRAE HVAC
inputs, ASTM E119 lab reports, and construction-industry submittals. The values below are the firm-blessed
conversion factors and shall be used verbatim; do not re-derive from memory at the desk.
• 1 psf = 47.88 Pa
• 1 psi = 6895 Pa
• 1 lb (force) = 4.448 N
• 1 in = 25.4 mm
• 1 ft = 0.3048 m
• 1 BTU/hr·ft² = 3.155 W/m²
• 1 K = 1 °C (for temperature differences only; not for absolute temperatures)
• T[K] = T[°C] + 273.15 (for absolute temperature conversion)
Two of the above deserve emphasis. First, the psf-to-Pa factor is 47.88, not unity — a psf value carried into a Pa field
without applying the factor is off by nearly two orders of magnitude, which is precisely the failure mode this SOP
exists to prevent. Second, the temperature-difference identity (1 K = 1 °C) applies only to differences; a rise of 139 °C
is a rise of 139 K, but an absolute temperature of 139 °C is 412.15 K, not 139 K.
Additional conversions not listed above shall be sourced from the NIST SP 811 tables and cited by page in the
analyst's worksheet. Conversion factors quoted from web calculators, textbook back-covers, or LLM outputs shall not
be used.

4. Sanity Check Requirement
 Every reported field value shall be sanity-checked against the governing boundary conditions of the load case it
belongs to before rollup. Reviewers shall confirm this check on the peer-review checklist (item 9). A pressure reported
at a scale inconsistent with the case boundary conditions is a defect regardless of unit label.
The check is a scale check, not a unit check. A pressure field whose header reads "Pa" but whose values sit at a
magnitude the boundary conditions cannot produce is defective even if the string "Pa" is technically the intended unit;
the label alone does not vindicate the number. The check is performed at three points in the workflow: (a) by the
case-setup engineer immediately after the first converged or first fully-transient output is produced, (b) by the rollup
engineer at the moment values move from raw fields into summary tables, and (c) by the reviewer at peer review. The
reviewer's confirmation is recorded against item 9 of the peer-review checklist for that project.
Sanity checks are performed against the boundary conditions of the same load case. Cross-case checks are
governed separately by Section 5.

5. Cross-Case Cross-Checks
A structural wind-load case and a fire or plume exposure case on the same engagement are often
distinct load cases with pressure scales that differ substantially from one another. A value
reported from one case shall not be checked against the boundary conditions of the other.
This restriction exists because multiple load cases often coexist on the same project
and their pressure fields are stored in the same case-folder hierarchy. A reviewer who reaches for the wildfire
boundary conditions when sanity-checking a structural wind pressure — or vice versa — will incorrectly clear values
that belong to the other case, or incorrectly flag values that were correct all along. Each case has its own boundary
conditions and its own expected scale, and each is sanity-checked only against its own.
Where a report presents results from both cases, the report body shall separate them under clearly labeled

    4. ASTM E119 vs WUI — Interpretive Note
             E119 endurance is a comparative assembly rating under standard fire exposure. It is not a
             prediction of wildfire survival time. A validation against E119 data validates a model against
             E119, not against a wildfire performance claim.

    The distinction matters in practice because the same physical wall assembly may carry both an E119 endurance
    number (in minutes to the governing thermal-transmission criterion) and a separate CFD-derived wildfire
    exposure result (peak unexposed-face temperature under a Sonoran buffelgrass fire matrix, say). The two are
    answers to two different questions and may not be interchanged.
    Specifically:
         An E119 furnace fire follows the standard time-temperature curve. A wildfire, wildland-urban interface, or
         facade fire does not. Their radiative fluxes on the exposed face, their gas temperatures, their duration, and
         their variability in time are all different.
         An E119 test rates the assembly against a defined standard fire; the resulting endurance number is
         comparable across assemblies tested against the same standard. It is not portable to any specific real-world
         fire.
         A validation of a CFD model against E119 data establishes that the model reproduces the assembly’s
         behaviour under the standard E119 exposure, within the reported E ± u_val. It says nothing about the model’s
         accuracy under a wildfire boundary condition, which is a different physical regime.
    Statements of the form “the assembly survives a wildfire for X minutes” or “the model is validated for wildfire
    performance” are not supported by an E119 comparison alone and must not appear in a firm deliverable on the
    basis of an E119 validation. If the firm wishes to make a wildfire-performance claim, it must be validated against
    wildfire-relevant test data under the same framework in Section 2.

cases in scope.
Wall functions at solid boundaries shall be the OpenFOAM standard high-Reynolds treatment appropriate to the SGS
closure and the local y+ range. The mesh at solid walls shall be sized so that the first-cell y+ stays within the
recommended band for the chosen wall function across the design range of the flow, and this shall be verified after
the initial transient by inspection of the wall-shear field.

6. Multi-Region Conjugate Heat Transfer for Cavity-Wall Assemblies
Fire-exposed building assemblies in the firm's project portfolio are commonly double-wythe (double-leaf) cavity
constructions with a solid outer leaf, an internal air cavity, and a solid inner leaf. The two leaves are typically
connected by discrete metallic ties (galvanized-steel truss ties or comparable) at regular vertical spacing, embedded
some distance into each leaf. These ties are a metallic thermal bridge across the assembly and, in ASTM E119
practice, they set the single-point temperature-rise criterion.
For any such assembly under a design fire, the CFD case shall be a multi-region conjugate heat transfer setup,
not a single-region simulation with lumped-wall boundary conditions. The following region topology is mandatory:
1. Outer leaf — solid region. Temperature-dependent k, rho, cp per the firm concrete table. Cell size at the
fire-exposed face fine enough to resolve the thermal boundary layer. 2. Cavity — fluid region with participating
radiation. Air properties temperature-dependent; radiation solved with fvDOM as in Section 3; cavity emissivities set
from the firm assembly library. 3. Inner leaf — solid region. Same treatment as the outer leaf. 4. Ties — each metallic
tie is a separate solid region, geometrically embedded through both leaves and terminating in the cavity air. Ties are
not represented as a smeared conductivity on the leaf regions and are not omitted. Steel k, rho, cp are
temperature-dependent over the design temperature range.
Region-to-region coupling at every solid–solid and solid–fluid interface shall use the OpenFOAM chtMultiRegion*
coupled boundary conditions with matched temperature and heat flux across the interface. Contact resistance at
tie-concrete embedments shall be applied when a firm-approved value is available; where no value is available,
perfect thermal contact is the conservative default for single-point temperature-rise prediction.
 Mesh refinement. Refinement zones shall be defined at every tie–concrete interface, so that the concentrated
conduction into the tie is captured with cell dimensions at least a factor of four finer than the bulk leaf mesh at the
embedment. Failure to refine at tie–concrete interfaces has been observed in past casework to underpredict the
single-point temperature rise and thereby to overpredict endurance; rev 4 mandates the refinement to eliminate that
failure mode.

7. Cross-Regime Transfer
Validated status attaches to a case within an envelope, not to a directory. A case is validated for the physical
regime, the boundary conditions, the fuel model, the geometry, and the solver package under which it was verified
against a reference. Copying the case directory to a new project and changing the geometry does not carry the
validation with the copy.
Geometry and mesh topology are regime-independent: a well-formed hexahedral mesh of a printed-concrete wall
assembly is a well-formed mesh whether the outer boundary condition is a fire, a wind load, or a room-air HVAC inlet.
Physics, however, is regime-dependent. When the regime changes, the following shall be rebuilt from first principles
and not carried across:
• Freestream and inlet conditions (wind speed, direction, roughness, ambient temperature, humidity).
• Solver selection (fireFoam vs. non-reacting solver vs. steady HVAC solver vs. compressible aerodynamics
   solver).
• Combustion model (present with EDC, absent, or substituted per Section 3).
• Radiation model (fvDOM with participating media, absent, or reduced-order).
• Turbulence closure (LES SGS choice, RANS, hybrid — per the regime call).
• Thermophysical property treatment (temperature-dependent vs. constant).
Reuse is prohibited without full physics rebuild. In particular:
• A validated non-reacting external-aerodynamics case (e.g. from prior aerospace work) shall not be extended into
   a fire case by adding a heat-release term. The compressible non-reacting envelope does not overlap the
   reacting-buoyant envelope, and the freestream density, the inlet turbulence, the solver, and the closures all differ.
• A validated HVAC interior-building-airflow case (steady, low-velocity, no combustion, no radiation, adiabatic
   external walls) shall not be carried forward into any case in scope of this standard without a full physics rebuild.
   The HVAC envelope does not overlap the fire or plume regime; validated status in the former regime confers no
   validated status in the latter.
• A validated aerospace high-altitude compressible case shall not be pulled forward as the physics basis for a
   ground-level fire simulation.
Where a project geometry and a good mesh already exist from an earlier case in a different regime, they may be
retained and re-used; the physics on top of them shall be built new to this standard. Case-directory reuse without a
physics rebuild has been the root cause of firm rework in the past and rev 4 is explicit that it is not acceptable
practice.

8. Verification and Validation
Verification (numerical correctness of the solve) and validation (agreement with physical reference) are governed by
separate firm procedures and are not restated in full here.
• Mesh and time-step verification, LES resolution acceptance (D*/dx and Pope resolved-TKE tests), and the scope
   of applicability of Roache/Richardson grid-convergence-index methods shall follow the current revision of the firm
   QA Verification Standard — Mesh & Resolution. Engineers shall consult it before setting up any
   three-grid or resolution study; the scope statement in it governs which verification methods are permissible for
   LES versus for steady RANS work.
• Validation against physical reference - the E = S - D formulation, validation uncertainty u_val, and
   the firm acceptance criterion — shall follow the current revision of the firm Validation QA Procedure & Acceptance
   Criterion, which is itself aligned with ASME V&V 20. Certified third-party test reports are the required source
   of the reference value D; it governs the treatment of client-amended data.
 The verification and validation sections of any project report shall cite the current revision numbers of both standards in
force at the time the report is issued.

Engineer, LLC Subject: Structural Wind-Load Basis Memo (SOW §3.2) Prepared: 10/09/2025. Basis of the
structural wind-load extraction called out in SOW §3.2 — ASCE 7-22 procedure, site parameters, velocity pressure,
and wall design pressures for the Ocotillo Additive Structures wall assembly at the Avra Valley WUI site.


1. Purpose and scope
This memo restates, in the firm's own words, the ASCE 7-22 procedure applied to the structural wind-load extraction
required under Section 3.2 of the signed Statement of Work (executed 2025-10-08). The output of that
extraction is the set of design wind pressures on the Ocotillo double-wythe printed-concrete wall assembly at the Avra
Valley WUI site, expressed both in US customary units (psf) and in SI (Pa) per the firm's Units and Conversions SOP.
The scope of this memo is limited to the structural load case defined in Section 3.2 of the SOW. It is not the wildfire
exposure matrix defined in Section 3.1 of the same SOW; the two load cases are physically and procedurally distinct,
and — as recorded in §5 below — a pressure or velocity reported from one may not be used to check the boundary
conditions of the other. External standards referred to in this memo (ASCE 7-22 §26 and §27) are summarized under
the firm's single-user license per the External Standards Digest (rev 1); no proprietary text is reproduced.

2. Site parameters
The site is the Ocotillo Additive Structures Sonoran-Desert WUI parcel west of Tucson (Avra Valley), Pima County,
Arizona. Site parameters used to enter the ASCE 7-22 wind procedure are as follows.

The occupancy is ordinary and the structure does not fall within the definitions of Risk Category III or IV, so Risk
Category II governs. The Avra Valley parcel is open desert with scattered creosote, mesquite, and buffelgrass ground
cover extending well beyond 20·h upwind in all directions relevant to the design wind rose; there is no built or forested
surface roughness of the kind that would qualify the site as Exposure B, and the site is not on open water, so
Exposure C is the correct assignment per ASCE 7-22 §26.7.3.

3. Velocity pressure
The velocity pressure at mean roof height h = 6.4 m is computed per ASCE 7-22 Eq. 26.10-1:
q_z = 0.00256 · K_z · K_zt · K_e · V² = 0.00256 · 0.91 · 1.0 · 1.0 · (96)² = 21.5 psf. Per ASCE 7-22 the wind
directionality factor K_d is applied in the design pressure equation (not the velocity pressure equation).
Arithmetic check: 0.00256 × 0.91 = 0.0023296; × 96² = × 9216 = 21.469 psf, rounded to q_z = 21.5 psf. In SI, 21.5
psf × 47.88 Pa/psf ≈ 1029 Pa.

4. Windward wall design pressure
For the main wind-force resisting system on an enclosed rigid building, the wall pressure on the windward face is
taken as
p_w = q_z · G · C_p · K_d = 21.5 · 0.85 · 0.8 · 0.85 = 12.41 psf, reported as 12.4 psf, which is 594 Pa at 1 psf =
47.88 Pa.
Where:
• G = 0.85 — gust-effect factor for a rigid building (natural frequency > 1 Hz), ASCE 7-22 §26.11.1;
• C_p = 0.8 — external pressure coefficient for the windward wall of an enclosed building, ASCE 7-22 Figure

• K_d = 0.85 — as tabulated in §2.1a above.

5. Section 3.1 versus Section 3.2 — the two load cases must not be conflated
This load case (SOW §3.2) is separate from the Section 3.1 wildfire exposure matrix. Section 3.1 runs at 5–12 m/s
(11.2–26.8 mph), where the velocity pressure is approximately
q_z ~ 0.00256 · 0.91 · (11.2 to 26.8)² ~ 0.29 to 1.68 psf ~ 14-80 Pa,

[Normal] THE CFD ME   |   Tucson, Arizona   |   AZ PE #48213   |   CFDME-2025-041 rev A
[Normal] Interim Client Summary — Structural Wind-Load Case
[Normal] 1. Purpose
[Normal] This DRAFT is the interim client summary of the ASCE 7-22 structural wind-load extraction called out under SOW Section 3.2, and covers the pressure rollup produced from the wall-probe extraction run on 10/09/2025. The scope is limited to the standalone structural wind-load case; the Section 3.1 wildfire matrix is handled separately and is not addressed here.
[Normal] Section 3.2 asks the firm to develop the code-basis wall pressures at the OAS-WUI-01 envelope for a discrete-wind-speed check independent of the wildfire matrix, and to report peak pressures on windward, side, and leeward faces at probe locations laid out in the case verification plan. The values summarized below are drawn directly from the interim probe extraction (interim_wall_pressures.csv, 10/09/2025) with no post-processing beyond the peak rollup.
[Normal] 2. Case Description
[List Bullet] Basis of loading: ASCE 7-22 (Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures).
[List Bullet] Site: Tucson, Arizona (Ocotillo pilot envelope, OAS-WUI-01_revC geometry of record).
[List Bullet] Basic wind speed, V: 96 mph (Risk Category II mapped value for the Tucson site).
[List Bullet] Exposure category: C (open terrain with scattered obstructions, consistent with the Avra Valley WUI setting).
[List Bullet] Risk category: II.
[List Bullet] Mean roof height, h: 6.4 m.
[List Bullet] Directionality and topography factors and the velocity-pressure exposure coefficient are applied per ASCE 7-22 Chapter 26 at the mean roof height; wall pressure coefficients on windward, side, and leeward faces are taken from Chapter 27 (directional procedure, enclosed low-rise building) at the site aspect ratio.
[Normal] The probe grid used for peak extraction consists of ten windward probes spanning the windward face, five probes on each side wall (north and south), and five probes on the leeward face. Probe elevations are 0.8 m, 3.2 m, and 5.6 m above grade. All probe values reported are peak (envelope) values from the interim extraction.
[Normal] 3. Results
[Normal] The table below reproduces the peak pressures from the interim extraction file exactly as recorded.
[Normal] Sign convention: positive pressures act inward on the wall face; negative pressures indicate suction (outward). Values are peaks across the interim probe set; the full per-probe listing is retained in interim_wall_pressures.csv.
[Normal] 4. Discussion
[Normal] Taken at face value, the pressures returned by the interim rollup are negligible relative to the structural design demand envelope typically associated with the framing of a 6.4 m mean-roof-height enclosed building at a 96 mph basic wind speed in Exposure C. A 12.4 Pa peak windward pressure is a very small fraction of the wall loads that would ordinarily drive sizing of tie, header, and out-of-plane bending checks for a printed-concrete assembly of this scale, and the corresponding side-wall and leeward suctions (−9.5 Pa and −6.1 Pa peak) are similarly small.
[Normal] On that basis the interim reading is that the ASCE 7-22 wall loading, taken as extracted, does not govern the OAS-WUI-01 envelope. Wildfire-driven radiative and convective loading (SOW Section 3.1) and the E119 fire-endurance envelope remain the controlling design considerations for the assembly. No structural remediation of the OAS-WUI-01_revC envelope is indicated by this interim result.
[Normal] The client should treat these figures as provisional pending peer review under the firm's QA workflow. The values here are unchanged from the interim rollup and have not been checked against boundary-condition inputs or reconciled with the ASCE 7-22 velocity-pressure and pressure-coefficient hand calculation feeding the extraction; those cross-checks are open items on the peer-review checklist and will be addressed before the Phase 1 structural wind-load memo is issued.

[0] THE CFD ME

[1] Tucson, Arizona  |  AZ PE #48213  |  Firm-internal engineering record

[2] VALIDATION MEMORANDUM

[3] E119 Companion Simulation — Ocotillo Double-Wythe Printed-Concrete Wall Assembly

[5] 1. Purpose and straight answer

[6] This memorandum supplies the validation record required for §7 of Phase 1 rev B. It uses the E119 companion run as it stands, RBFMT-25-0918, IWFPE-CERT-25-0374, Ocotillo’s 10/09/2025 amended burn data, and drawing OAS_wall_assembly_section.png. No new runs or tests are used; nothing outside this memorandum is changed.

[7] The discrepancy is a resolved model error, not measurement scatter: |E| is larger than the combined uncertainty, and positive E means the model predicts more endurance than the certified test observed, which is unconservative in a rating context. No unqualified validation claim may be issued. The §7 stub cannot be completed as a validation; it can be completed only as the §5 rollup plus a documented finding and a rework plan. The 10/09/2025 request to describe the simulation as “validated against the certified test” is not supported by this record.

[8] The §7 stub’s S = 131 min stands as the prediction; its implication of validation does not. Section 7 must be rewritten around the §5 rollup and the §7 comparisons. This memorandum does not substitute D, change the certified rating, or assert wildfire performance.

[9] 2. Records relied on

[10] Paths are from the file-server root. All records were on file as of 10/10/2025 and none was altered for this memorandum.

[11] Table 2-1. Records relied on. Two records are missing and condition this memorandum (below).

[12] Missing record (a): no companion-run case record. There is no case-setup record, mesh, solver log, or resolution study for the E119 companion run; the only artifact is the results CSV. S can be read but not audited to Procedure §3, and no run identifier exists. Filing the record and assigning an identifier are conditions of closing §7.

[13] Missing record (b): no project-specific u_val tabulation. Procedure §4 requires a project-specific tabulation of u_num, u_inp, and u_exp in the project QA folder before u_val is published; none is on file. The u_val used here is the §4 class default: u_num = ±4 min, u_inp = ±6 min, u_exp = ±5 min, combined to ±8.77 min and reported as ±9 min. The tabulation must be filed before signature.

[14] 3. S — simulation prediction and how the crossing was read

[15] Governing criterion. ASTM E119 applies two thermal-transmission criteria, both measured as rises above initial ambient: the nine-thermocouple average rise of 139 °C and the single-point rise of 181 °C; the earlier governs (RBFMT-25-0918 §§1 and 5.3; Digest §1). In RBFMT-25-0918 the single-point criterion was reached first, at 118 min at TC-6 over a 3.8 mm tie course; the average criterion was reached at 163 min (§§3.2 and 5.1–5.3). The governing criterion is the single-point 181 °C rise; its certified time is 118 min.

[16] Run basis. The companion file has 181 data rows at 1 min cadence, t = 0–180 min. The t = 0 row is 21.0 °C in all five columns. The header cross-walks T_unexposed_avg_C to the §5.1 nine-TC average criterion and T_unexposed_max_C to the §5.2 single-point criterion at the unexposed face over the tie course. T_tie_C is a simulation-internal tie temperature with no direct RBFMT-25-0918 thermocouple equivalent; it is not the single-point analog, and using it gives a spurious 101 min crossing (Appendix A).

[17] Crossing times. The thresholds applied to the run are 139 °C + 21.0 °C = 160.0 °C absolute for the average criterion and 181 °C + 21.0 °C = 202.0 °C absolute for the single-point criterion. Linear interpolation between the two adjacent 1 min samples gives 130.9 min for the single-point criterion (reported 131 min) and 176.1 min for the average criterion (reported 176 min). Appendix A holds the arithmetic and the bracketing samples; the body reports the crossing times, not the samples. Applying 181 °C as an absolute temperature instead of a rise gives 117.6 min → 118 min; that is the wrong rule, and its coincidence with the test endurance must not be used.

[18] S = 131 min. The §7 stub’s number stands; its framing does not. The companion run has no run identifier; it is cited to the results file and SHA-256 b69ae8dbeb876080e0a421fa94200b0ffe9fef6f1ef10d731b5411575918d678. Assigning an identifier in the case record is a condition of closing §7.

[19] 4. D — experimental value adopted and disposition on Bianca’s figure

[20] D = 118 min (RBFMT-25-0918 §5.3: single-point at 118 min at TC-6; average at 163 min; the report is the certified test of record for IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.1). D is taken without adjustment.

[21] Bianca Rennert’s 129 min is not admissible as D. Ocotillo transmitted Validation/burn_data_original_vs_revised.csv with Ms. Rennert’s email of 10/09/2025 11:42, revising the single-point endurance from 118 min to 129 min on the basis of a post-test TC-6 calibration correction; the average remains 163 min. Procedure §6 requires all three of: (1) a reissued report RBFMT-25-0918-R1, signed by the laboratory’s authorized signatory, stating the reason for revision; (2) a calibration certificate covering TC-6, with a date and calibration-authority reference traceable to the correction; and (3) an explicit statement in the reissued report that the revised value supersedes the original for all downstream use. None of the three is on file.

[22] The in-force calibration record. RBFMT-25-0918 §7 lists RBFMT-CAL-25-0812-TC covering TC-1 through TC-10, calibrated 2025-08-12, NIST-traceable, in force on the 09/24/2025 test date, and covering the full observed temperature range. On the record as it stands, TC-6 was covered by an in-force calibration certificate. A client-side post-test correction is not a laboratory revision (Procedure §6). The transmittal is recorded in the correspondence folder, and D remains 118 min.

[23] Scale check and materiality. At the crossing the run’s maximum is rising at about 1.6 °C/min (200.5 °C at 130 min to 202.1 °C at 131 min), so an 11 min shift corresponds to roughly 18 °C of TC-6 correction — a large instrument correction that no certificate on file supports. At D = 129 min the rollup would read E = 131 min − 129 min = +2 min against a criterion of 12.9 min, and |E| = 2 min would sit inside u_val = 8.77 min; the numerical tests would be met. The 129 min also sits just below the 129.8 min clearing bound for the certified D. That is why Procedure §6 exists; it is not a reason to use 129 min.

[24] 5. Rollup, criterion, uncertainty, and the clearing bound

[25] This is the rollup the reviewer must be able to sign. It is in the Procedure §3 order, every value carries its unit, and limits are stated as they fall.

[26] Table 5-1. Validation rollup of record. |E| = 13 min exceeds both the 11.8 min criterion and the ±8.77 min validation uncertainty.

[27] Procedure §5 disposition. Because |E| exceeds both the criterion and u_val, the deliverable may not be released with an unqualified validation claim. This memorandum records a documented finding and calls for model rework; the remedy is not a substitution of D (Procedure §§6 and 8). The primary test fails by 1.2 min against 11.8 min; the secondary fails by 4.23 min against 8.77 min, or by 4 min against the reported ±9 min. Even if the criterion were rounded to 12 min, |E| = 13 min would still exceed it by 1 min.

[28] 6. Geometry — is the assembly in the run the one the certification covers?

[29] Answer: yes, on every parameter the certification tabulates. IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.2 tabulates nine parameters; the run geometry, OAS-WUI-01_revC, conforms on all nine.

[30] Table 6-1. Certified geometry against run geometry (IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.2). The first nine rows are the certification’s tabulated parameters; the tenth is an idealization, not a certified parameter.

[31] What that rests on. (1) The results-file header names OAS-WUI-01_revC and cross-walks its columns to RBFMT-25-0918 §5.1 and §5.2. (2) The revC property table carries the nine values above; revC is the geometry of record in SOW §2 and the deliverable manifest. (3) The snappyHexMesh log names OAS-WUI-01_revC.FCStd, records an export timestamp of 2025-10-08 16:42:11 -0700 (received with the signed SOW), and records a mesh build on 10/09/2025 from 07:14 to 10:26 MST. (4) revD was received on 10/09/2025 at 16:12, after the mesh build; it is not the geometry in the run. (5) The dimensioned drawing OAS_wall_assembly_section.png carries drawing ID OAS-WA-305mm-DW and is identified as the same assembly in scoping memo §6 and Phase 1 rev B §3.5.

[32] Two qualifications. First, panel plan size is not a certified parameter: the tested specimen was 3.05 m × 3.05 m and the model panel is 1830 mm × 2745 mm, so conformance rests on the layup and tie schedule, not on panel dimensions. The difference is a geometric idealization and belongs in u_inp. Second, revD is not covered: its 610 mm parapet, 3355 mm total height, 50 mm coping, and 25 mm drip overhang are deviations from the tabulated geometry and fall outside IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.2. revD is not in the run; it is a geometry revision superseding the geometry of record, and SOW §8 requires an executed change order before any work on it. No such change order is on file. The certification is also limited to the §1.3 conditions: non-load-bearing, standard E119 curve, no applied load, no hose-stream retest (Ironwood §§5.3–5.4).

[33] 7. The two comparisons, what they say, and the rework

[34] The two requested comparisons are the separation between the criteria in the test against the same separation in the run, and the distance from the governing point to the nine-point mean at governance in each.

[35] Table 7-1. The two diagnostic comparisons. Times are to the nearest minute; the unrounded separation is shown once.

[36] What they say. The separation is preserved to 0.2 min (0.4 %), and the model’s tie hot-spot excess is slightly larger than the test’s (+6.2 °C, +7 %). The model captures which criterion governs, why it governs, and in what order; the tie-bridge single-point mechanism is not mis-modelled and the tie path is not under-represented. Both criteria are late by the same 13 min. A near-pure translation in time points to a uniform bias in the whole-assembly thermal response or in the imposed exposure, not a local mechanism error. It is not a reason to adjust D.

[37] Where the rework belongs. In the companion model, not in D and not in the wildfire matrix. First, a documented case-setup record and u_num evidence must be created; neither exists today. Then, per Modeling Standard rev 4: a multi-region CHT treatment with each tie a separate solid region and refinement zones at every tie–concrete interface at least a factor of four finer than the bulk leaf mesh (§6); temperature-dependent k, ρ, and cp for solids (§3.5); cavity radiation by fvDOM with concrete and steel emissivities of 0.90 and 0.25 (dimensionless; App. A); and a furnace-side exposure audit against the E119 gas-temperature history actually delivered (Digest §1). Without the case record the 13 min cannot be attributed further; the diagnostics do not support a local tie-mechanism error and point instead to the bulk thermal response or the exposure.

[38] Has it started? No. No setup file, mesh, solver log, verification study, or rework note for the companion run exists on file. CO-001 (marketing animation, 12 h, $2,400) and CO-002 (mesh refinement on wildfire cases 240°/8 m/s and 270°/8 m/s, 30 h, $6,750) were executed 10/09/2025, but neither touches the companion model. The budget shows the reviewer commission ($4,225) and contingency ($8,000) unspent and HPC actual at $2,100 of $6,200. The only October solve on file is attempt 3 of the wildfire model (6 h 41 min wall clock, 64 cores, 424.3 CPU-hours), not the companion and itself nonconforming (§10). The Q3 cluster export ends 09/30/2025 with no CFDME-2025-041 jobs; it neither evidences nor excludes October compute.

[39] 8. What this establishes about the wildfire claim, and what would close the gap

[40] What the exercise establishes. At most, the comparison supports a mechanistic reading of E119 thermal-transmission behaviour: the single-point criterion governs, the two criteria are separated by 45 min in both the test and the run, and the tie hot-spot is present and slightly larger in the model. That is useful model-diagnostic information. It is not a validation: the numerical tests in §5 are not met even for E119, and S comes from a run with no documented case record.

[41] What it does not establish. It does not establish wildfire performance, wildfire survival time, or the marketing proposition that the assembly is “more fire-resistant than wood-frame construction in a Sonoran WUI wildfire.” There is no wildfire-exposure physical test on the project, no wood-frame comparator test, and no certified D for a wildfire exposure. ASTM E119 is a comparative assembly rating under the standard furnace curve, not a WUI exposure (Procedure §7; Digest §4; Ironwood §5.2; SOW §7). The finding does not extend to any layup other than revC, to loaded configurations, or to hose-stream criteria (Ironwood §§5.3–5.4).

[42] What would close the gap. Three things: (i) one or more certified third-party wildfire-exposure tests of the same assembly, with wind-driven radiant and convective exposure and measured incident heat flux, gas temperature, and unexposed-face and tie temperatures at the same instrument locations; if the claim remains comparative, a paired wood-frame specimen tested in the same campaign; (ii) a companion wildfire CFD run in that configuration; and (iii) a validation under Procedure rev 2 using D from that certified report. Anything less leaves the claim as a proposition, not a validated result.

[43] Required reporting form for any future comparison. Report S, D, E, and u_val, in that order, in a single line or table, each with its unit, citing the run identifier and the certified report number and clause. Then state the criterion (10 % of D) and both secondary comparisons: |E| against u_val, and the sign of E against the physical expectation. Never a yes/no; never “matches,” “agrees,” “confirms,” “is validated,” or “within tolerance” in place of the numbers (Procedure §3; Digest §2). The u_val build must be project-specific: u_num from an LES resolution study meeting D*/dx in the 5–10 band (dimensionless) and Pope resolved-TKE ≥ 80 % (Verification Standard rev 3 §5), u_inp from fuel, boundary-condition, and geometry uncertainty, and u_exp from the wildfire test instrumentation. A compliant line reads: “S = ___ min; D = ___ min; E = ___ min; u_val = ___ min (u_num ___ min, u_inp ___ min, u_exp ___ min); criterion = ___ min (10 % of D); |E| vs criterion ___; |E| vs u_val ___; sign ___.”

[44] 9. Bianca’s figure and the certified rating

[45] If the 129 min were ever substantiated by a reissued RBFMT-25-0918-R1 with a TC-6 calibration certificate and an explicit supersession statement, the governing single-point endurance would move to 129 min. That clears the 120 min 2-hour rung by 9 min; the current certified 118 min falls 2 min short (Ironwood §3). It would therefore support a 2-hour fire-resistance rating on the same non-load-bearing, no-hose-stream basis. It would also change this rollup to E = 131 min − 129 min = +2 min against a criterion of 12.9 min, with |E| = 2 min inside u_val = 8.77 min; the numerical tests would be met. A D of 129 min leaves only 0.8 min of margin below the 129.8 min prediction that would clear the criterion against the certified D; that sensitivity is why Procedure §6 exists, not a reason to depart from it.

[46] Who may act. Only Red Butte can reissue the report, and only Ironwood Fire Protection Engineering — Marla Kettering, PE, AZ PE #45106 — can certify or restate the rating. Ironwood §4 is explicit: “No other party may certify or restate this rating.” The CFD ME is not entitled to act: a validation finding is not a rating action (Procedure §9), and the SOW excludes any determination of ratings, listings, or certifications (SOW §§1, 8, and 10). Ocotillo marketing may not restate the rating either. This memorandum records Ocotillo’s request and the admissibility test; it makes no request of Red Butte or Ironwood and takes no position on the rating. Stamp language (verbatim): “CFD thermal analysis only. Fire-resistance rating certified separately by others.”

[47] 10. What this means for the rest of Phase 1

[48] Phase 1 rev B §7 and §8. Section 7 can be closed only as a documented finding, not as a validation. Section 8 conclusions cannot use “validated.” Phase 1 rev B cannot be issued for client transmission on the current record.

[49] The six-case wildfire matrix is not conforming as set up. The only filed case-setup record is the DWA aerospace template: steady rhoSimpleFoam, k-omega SST RANS, no combustion, no radiation, adiabatic walls, no conjugate regions, and aerospace reference conditions of 26,500 Pa, 223 K, and 0.4 kg/m³. Attempt 3 partially rebuilt to fireFoam with EDC and fvDOM, but runs the fire solver in a forced steady SIMPLE loop (a single outer corrector, nOuterCorrectors = 1), with k-epsilon RANS and time interpreted as iteration count; the live controlDict still has adjustTimeStep no, endTime 2000 (iteration count), and writeControl timeStep, and the run stalled in a limit cycle. That record, taken as a whole, does not conform to Modeling Standard rev 4 §§3.1–3.6, 4, 5, 6, and 7. The matrix must be rebuilt before the 10/20/2025 LES setup memo and 11/07/2025 delivery; this is the dominant schedule risk, ahead of the companion rework.

[50] 270° is not new scope. The signed SOW §3.1 matrix already contains 270° at 5, 8, and 12 m/s as cases 3.1-D, 3.1-E, and 3.1-F. The 10/09/2025 request for a “second direction” does not require a change order; SOW §8 makes only directions beyond 240° and 270° out of scope. The change-order discussion should be corrected on that point.

[51] revD must not be picked up. It requires (a) an executed change order under SOW §8 and (b) recognition that it is outside IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 and would need a new test and a new certification before any rating statement.

[52] The 10/27/2025 Red Butte window is a confirmatory ASTM E119 test (SOW §5), not a wildfire-phase physical test. Phase 1 rev B §4.2 and the staffing assignment “Red Butte confirmatory ASTM E119 test for Ocotillo Phase 1 wildfire assembly” misdescribe it. At most it supplies a second independent E119 dataset for a repeat comparison.

[53] Independent structural wind-load defect. The interim summary reports 12.4 Pa windward, but the wind-load basis memo §4 computes 12.4 psf = 594 Pa (Units SOP §3); this unit-carry defect keeps checklist item 9 open and must be corrected before issue.

[54] Launch timing. It is a commercial constraint and cannot move a validation outcome; no number or claim goes into the press deck until the rework is complete and re-reported.

- **`output/CFDME-2025-041_validation_crossing_calc_revA.csv`** — 35-row unit-bearing crossing and rollup worksheet.

**Key results unchanged**

The companion simulation **does not validate**:

- **S = 131 min** — single-point analog crossed at 130.9 min.
- **D = 118 min** — RBFMT-25-0918 §5.3.
- **E = +13 min**.
- Acceptance criterion: **11.8 min** (10 % of D).
- Validation uncertainty: **±8.77 min**, reported **±9 min**.
- **|E| exceeds both** — by 1.2 min against the criterion and 4.23 min against the unrounded uncertainty. This is a resolved model error, not scatter.
- Largest prediction clearing the criterion: **129.8 min**, or **129 min or less** in whole minutes.

Geometry: revC conforms to all nine parameters in IWFPE-CERT-25-0374 §1.2. revD is outside the certification and requires an executed change order; panel plan size is a non-certified geometric idealization.

Bianca’s **129 min is inadmissible as D** — no reissued RBFMT-25-0918-R1, no TC-6 calibration certificate, no supersession statement. If substantiated, it would support a 2-hour rating, but only Red Butte and Ironwood can act.

Comparisons: test separation **45 min** versus run **45.2 min**; governing-point excess **≈85 °C** versus **91.2 °C**. The uniform 13 min lag points to a whole-assembly or exposure bias; rework belongs in the companion model and has not been started.
